classes.qualifier-missing-from-name: the definition adds an identifying attribute the name lacks (normalisation, a vector or component where the name states a scalar, an ion-only population where the name states an element, a reference-relative value, an equivalent-electron count, an averaged form, extra weighting), so the name alone denotes a broader or different quantity
classes.definition-narrower-than-name: the definition restricts applicability to a subset of the objects the name covers (a coil family, an instrument, a plasma regime or surface, a layer)
classes.abstract-parent-as-quantity: the definition declares a parent, umbrella or structural quantity whose population, component, averaging or specialised forms are fixed by more specific instances
classes.unit-does-not-fit-name: the unit's physical dimension contradicts the quantity the name states
classes.agrees: the definition states the same scope the name states

items.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description:
Signed toroidal projection of the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic fluid
velocity for one ion charge state in the edge plasma, distinct from
individual guiding-center motion.
items.documentation:
The toroidal ion charge-state diamagnetic-drift velocity is the signed
projection of the pressure-gradient-driven fluid drift for one ion charge
state in the edge plasma. It represents a fluid-moment contribution rather
than the guiding-center motion of individual ions.

For a magnetized ion charge state labeled $\alpha$ with scalar partial
pressure, the defining projection is:

$$
v_{\ast\alpha,\phi} = \left(-\frac{\nabla p_\alpha \times \mathbf{B}}{q_\alpha n_\alpha B^2}\right)\cdot\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $v_{\ast\alpha,\phi}$ is the toroidal diamagnetic-drift velocity
component, $p_\alpha$ is the charge state's partial pressure, $\nabla
p_\alpha$ is its pressure gradient, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field
vector, $B=|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, $q_\alpha$ is the signed particle
charge, $n_\alpha$ is the charge-state number density, and
$\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the unit vector toward increasing toroidal
angle. The right-handed cylindrical frame is $(R,\phi,Z)$, where $R$ is
distance from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height.

Only the specified ion species and charge state are included; no averaging
over charge states or species is implied. This contribution excludes
electric-field drift, polarization drift, curvature drift, and independent
parallel flow. Although the diamagnetic drift vector is perpendicular to the
magnetic field, its geometric toroidal component need not vanish.

The species-level [ion velocity due to diamagnetic
drift](name:ion_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) is the density-weighted
mean over all ionic charge states of that species. Its toroidal projection
is therefore the density-weighted mean of the corresponding charge-state
toroidal components, not their sum.

Sign convention: Positive when the diamagnetic fluid drift of the specified
ion charge state has a component toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in
the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: radiative_ordinary_mode_temperature_at_ece_channel
items.description:
Predicted equivalent blackbody temperature of ordinary-mode electron
cyclotron emission at a frequency-selective ECE channel.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the equivalent blackbody temperature associated with
radiation emitted in the ordinary polarization mode of electron cyclotron
emission. It represents the theoretically predicted O-mode emission
intensity rather than the kinetic temperature of the electron population.

The radiation temperature is defined by equating the ordinary-mode spectral
radiance to that of a blackbody at the same frequency:

$$
I_{\nu}^{\mathrm{O}} = B_{\nu}\!\left(T_{\mathrm{rad}}^{\mathrm{O}}\right)
$$

where $I_{\nu}^{\mathrm{O}}$ is the predicted ordinary-mode spectral
radiance, $B_{\nu}$ is the blackbody spectral-radiance function, $\nu$ is
the channel frequency, and $T_{\mathrm{rad}}^{\mathrm{O}}$ is the
corresponding ordinary-mode radiation temperature.

The quantity applies specifically to ordinary-mode propagation at the
frequency-selective ECE channel and is not a sum or average over
polarization modes or channel frequencies. It is distinct from the
extraordinary-mode radiation temperature, represented by [radiative
extraordinary-mode temperature at an ECE
channel](name:radiative_extraordinary_mode_temperature_at_ece_channel), and
from the mode-agnostic [radiative temperature at an ECE
channel](name:radiative_temperature_at_ece_channel).

items.name: power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination
items.description:
Total power deposited on a divertor target by recombination processes,
summing the plasma-ion and neutral-particle recombination channels at the
plasma-material interface.
items.documentation:
This quantity captures the combined recombination power delivered to a
single divertor target, encompassing two physically distinct contributions:
energy released when plasma ions recombine at or near the target surface
(the plasma channel, quantified by
plasma_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination) and energy deposited
when neutral particles undergo recombination into lower-energy bound states
at the material wall (the neutral channel, quantified by
[neutral_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination](name:neutral_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination)).

The total recombination power at the target decomposes additively:

$$
P_{\rm rec,target} = P_{\rm rec,plasma} + P_{\rm rec,neutral}
$$

where $P_{\rm rec,plasma}$ is the ion-recombination contribution and $P_{\rm
rec,neutral}$ is the neutral-particle recombination contribution, both in W.

This target-localized quantity is a spatial specialization of the
volume-integrated
[power_due_to_recombination](name:power_due_to_recombination), which
integrates recombination power over the full plasma domain. In attached
divertor operation, recombination power at the target is a minor fraction of
the total heat load; in detached or high-recycling regimes, surface and
volumetric recombination become significant energy sinks that reduce the
conducted and convected flux reaching the target. It is inferred from edge
plasma simulations or from particle flux measurements combined with surface
energy-release models, and is non-negative by definition.

items.name: momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential
items.description:
Dimensionless toroidal plasma-momentum flux contribution driven by the
perturbed parallel electromagnetic vector potential in gyrokinetic
turbulence, generalized across parallel and perpendicular velocity-space
channels.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the normalized contribution to toroidal plasma-momentum
transport produced by fluctuations of the perturbed parallel electromagnetic
vector potential in gyrokinetic turbulence. It represents transport across
an oriented surface, not local momentum density or the total momentum
contained in a volume.

The normalization is defined by

$$
\Pi_{\delta A_\parallel}^{\mathrm{norm}} = \frac{\Pi_{\delta A_\parallel}}{\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $\Pi_{\delta A_\parallel}^{\mathrm{norm}}$ is the normalized quantity,
$\Pi_{\delta A_\parallel}$ is the toroidal momentum-flux contribution driven
by the perturbed parallel electromagnetic vector potential, and
$\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the positive reference momentum-flux scale. The
subscript $\delta A_\parallel$ identifies the perturbed parallel
electromagnetic vector potential.

Toroidal momentum refers to the direction of increasing toroidal angle
$\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is
major radius and $Z$ is vertical height. This parent is agnostic to
velocity-space projection and covers both the parallel and perpendicular
channel contributions without selecting either channel or requiring that the
channels be summed.

The quantity excludes momentum-flux contributions attributed to other
fluctuation mechanisms and is distinct from local momentum density, total
momentum in a volume, and the channel-resolved [parallel momentum-flux
contribution](name:parallel_momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential)
or [perpendicular momentum-flux
contribution](name:perpendicular_momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential).
It is also distinct from the normalized contribution driven by a perturbed
parallel magnetic field.

This quantity is the normalized, driver-specific specialization of [momentum
flux due to the perturbed parallel vector
potential](name:momentum_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential).
The normalization changes the reference scale while preserving the signed
character of the underlying momentum-flux contribution.

items.name: electron_source_rate_at_pellet_path_due_to_pellet_injection
items.description:
Electron source rate at the pellet path due to pellet injection is the
charge-weighted electron-equivalent production rate from ablation and
ionization of pellet material at a specified position along the injected
pellet trajectory.
items.documentation:
Electron source rate at the pellet path due to pellet injection is the
charge-weighted electron-equivalent production rate from ablation and
ionization of pellet material at a specified position along the injected
pellet trajectory. It counts the free-electron source associated with
material reaching that path position, not the electron concentration of the
surrounding plasma.

For trajectory coordinate $\ell$ and time $t$, the local rate is defined by
the charge-weighted sum over ablated pellet constituents contributing at
that same path position:

$$
S_e(\ell,t) = \sum_a Z_a^\mathrm{eff}(\ell,t)\,\dot{N}_a(\ell,t)
$$

where $S_e$ is the electron source rate at the pellet path due to pellet
injection, $a$ indexes the pellet constituents or represented charge-state
groups, $\dot{N}_a$ is the local production rate of constituent $a$ by
ablation and ionization, and $Z_a^\mathrm{eff}$ is the effective number of
free electrons contributed by one produced constituent. For a fully ionized
atomic constituent, $Z_a^\mathrm{eff}$ reduces to its nuclear charge.

This is a path-position rate, not a source density per distance along the
pellet trajectory or a volume-integrated source. The [electron source rate
due to injection](name:electron_source_rate_due_to_injection) is obtained
only after aggregating the appropriate local electron-equivalent
contributions, while electron density of pellet path describes electron
concentration along the same trajectory. The [accumulated particle count at
pellet path due to pellet
injection](name:accumulated_particle_count_at_pellet_path_due_to_pellet_injection)
is an unweighted cumulative particle count; it is not an electron-equivalent
accumulated source unless the same charge weighting and time integration are
applied.

The value is non-negative and is zero where injected pellet material at the
considered path position does not produce free electrons.

items.name: area_of_toroidal_field_coil
items.description:
Non-negative geometric area of the conducting material within a
toroidal-field-coil conductor’s cross-sectional boundary, measured normal to
its local centerline.
items.documentation:
The area of a toroidal-field-coil conductor is the geometric area occupied
by conducting material in a cross-section normal to the conductor’s local
centerline. It excludes any void, bore, insulation, or surrounding aperture.

The area is defined by

$$
A_{\mathrm{cond}} = \iint_{S_{\mathrm{cond}}} dS
$$

where $A_{\mathrm{cond}}$ is the conductor cross-sectional area,
$S_{\mathrm{cond}}$ is the region enclosed by the conductor boundary, and
$dS$ is its differential area element.

This quantity complements the conductor dimensions represented by the [width
of the toroidal field coil](name:width_of_toroidal_field_coil) and [height
of the toroidal field coil](name:height_of_toroidal_field_coil); it is not
the area enclosed by a winding or loop.

items.name: source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
items.description:
Instantaneous equivalent-electron source rate delivered to the plasma vessel
by gas injection systems, where each injected atom contributes Z equivalent
electrons per second according to its atomic number.
items.documentation:
The source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous rate at
which neutral gas is admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection
hardware, expressed as an equivalent-electron count rate. Every injected
atom of atomic number $Z$ contributes $Z$ equivalent electrons per second to
the total inventory rate, providing a unified accounting framework across
species of differing nuclear charge.

The defining relation for a single injected species is:

$$
\dot{S} = Z \cdot \dot{N}_{\mathrm{atoms}}
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{atoms}}$ is the raw atomic delivery rate in atoms
per second and $Z$ is the atomic number of the injected species. For
simultaneous multi-species injection, contributions are summed over all
active species.

This rate is inferred from calibrated mass-flow controllers or upstream
pressure-rise measurements on the gas supply plumbing. It is the
instantaneous time derivative of the corresponding accumulated
equivalent-electron inventories, such as
[accumulated_argon_count](name:accumulated_argon_count) or
accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection. The nearest-peer quantity
gas_particle_source_rate_over_vessel_due_to_gas_injection provides the
vessel-integrated analog expressed in raw gas-phase particles rather than
equivalent electrons.

items.name: effective_area_of_langmuir_probe
items.description:
Effective collection area of a Langmuir probe, obtained by projecting its
plasma-facing collector surface onto the plane normal to the local magnetic
field.
items.documentation:
The effective area of a Langmuir probe is the plasma-facing collector
surface area projected onto the plane perpendicular to the local
magnetic-field direction. It represents the area governing particle
collection when the sheath is magnetized.

$$
A_{\mathrm{eff}} = \int_{S_{\mathrm{w}}} \left|\hat{\mathbf{n}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}\right|\,dA
$$

where $A_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the effective collection area, $S_{\mathrm{w}}$
is the plasma-exposed collector surface, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the local
outward unit normal, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the local magnetic-field unit
vector, and $dA$ is an element of collector surface area. The absolute dot
product gives the geometrical projection factor.

Unlike the total area of a Langmuir probe, this quantity accounts for
magnetic-field orientation; unlike the [wetted area of a Langmuir
probe](name:wetted_area_of_langmuir_probe), it is not the unprojected
plasma-exposed surface area.

items.name: poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_beam_tracing_point
items.description:
Signed poloidal magnetic flux function evaluated at a beam-tracing point,
serving as the magnetic-surface label at that location.
items.documentation:
Poloidal magnetic flux at a beam-tracing point is the value of the
equilibrium flux function at the point where the ray or beam path intersects
the plasma. In an axisymmetric equilibrium, it labels the nested magnetic
surface passing through that point and is distinct from the normalized
coordinate derived from axis and boundary values.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the flux function is
defined by

$$
\psi(R,Z) = \int_0^R B_Z(R',Z)\,2\pi R'\,dR'
$$

where $R$ is major radius, $Z$ is vertical height, $R'$ is the integration
radius, and $B_Z$ is the vertical magnetic-field component. The beam-tracing
point supplies the coordinates at which $\psi$ is evaluated. Its value is
related to [poloidal magnetic flux at a flux
surface](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_flux_surface), while [normalized
poloidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate) uses the
magnetic-axis and plasma-boundary flux values for normalization.

Sign convention: Positive when $B_Z$ on the integration disk points in the
$+Z$ direction.

items.name: volume_averaged_neutral_species_density
items.description:
Mean number density of a specified neutral species over the plasma volume
enclosed by the last closed flux surface during plasma initiation.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the spatial mean of the local number density of one
specified neutral species within the plasma volume enclosed by the last
closed flux surface during plasma initiation. The local quantity is
distinguished from [neutral_density](name:neutral_density), which is
evaluated at a point.

$$
\overline{n}_0 = \frac{1}{V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}} \int_{V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}} n_0(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $n_0(\mathbf{r})$ is the local number density of the specified neutral
species at position $\mathbf{r}$, $V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is the volume enclosed
by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is the volume element.

The average is species-specific and excludes neutral particles outside the
enclosed volume. It is not the charge-state or population aggregate
represented by [total_neutral_density](name:total_neutral_number_density),
nor the volume average of ion density represented by
[volume_averaged_ion_density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density).

items.name: thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Thermal electron torque density due to collisions is the local
angular-momentum transfer rate per volume delivered to thermal electrons by
Coulomb collisions with fast particles.
items.documentation:
Thermal electron torque density due to collisions is the local
angular-momentum transfer rate per volume delivered to the thermal electron
population by Coulomb collisions with fast particles.

Its vector form is related to the collisional momentum-transfer density by

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{r}) = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{R}_{e,\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{r})
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the torque-density vector,
$\mathbf{r}$ is the displacement from the torque origin, and
$\mathbf{R}_{e,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional momentum-transfer density
acting on thermal electrons.

The quantity is independent of orbit-class and component selection;
co-passing, counter-passing, trapped, and directional forms are specialized
instances. It is distinct from the broader [electron torque density due to
collisions](name:electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions) and includes the
[toroidal thermal electron torque density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
as a component-resolved form. Torque transferred to fast particles is
excluded.

Sign convention: Positive when a component of
$\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{coll}}$ points toward increasing $R$,
increasing $\phi$, or increasing $Z$, respectively, in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: poloidal_magnetic_field_of_magnetic_field_probe
items.description:
Poloidal magnetic field of a magnetic-field probe is the signed local
poloidal magnetic-field value represented by a poloidal field probe after
its nonlinear response calibration, sensed in the R-Z plane of the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Poloidal magnetic field of a magnetic-field probe is the signed local
poloidal magnetic-field value represented by a poloidal field probe after
its nonlinear response calibration. The sensed component lies in the $R$-$Z$
plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The defining relation applies the probe's nonlinear calibration curve to the
linearly calibrated projection of the local field onto the probe's sensitive
direction:

$$
B_{\mathrm{probe}} = f_{\mathrm{nl}}\!\left(\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{probe}} \cdot \mathbf{B}(\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{probe}})\right)
$$

where $B_{\mathrm{probe}}$ is this quantity,
$\mathbf{B}(\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{probe}})$ is the local [magnetic-field
vector](name:magnetic_field) at the probe sensing position
$\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{probe}}$, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{probe}}$ is the
unit vector along the probe's positive poloidal sensitive direction in the
$R$-$Z$ plane, and $f_{\mathrm{nl}}$ is the probe's nonlinear calibration
curve, which maps the linearly calibrated field value to the field value
corrected for nonlinear sensor response such as Hall-sensor saturation or
hysteresis. Where the sensor responds linearly, $f_{\mathrm{nl}}$ reduces to
the identity and the quantity equals the plain projection.

Scope is limited to an individual probe and to the point or small sensing
volume it represents; no averaging over multiple probes, flux surfaces, or
spatial regions is implied. The probe's position in the poloidal plane is
given by the [radial coordinate of the poloidal magnetic-field
probe](name:radial_coordinate_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe) and the
[vertical coordinate of the poloidal magnetic-field
probe](name:vertical_coordinate_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe). The
[toroidal angle of a poloidal magnetic-field
probe](name:toroidal_angle_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe) characterizes
the orientation of the probe's sensitive axis and is not a spatial
coordinate of this quantity's locus.

This quantity is a single signed poloidal component: it is not the toroidal
component, not the magnitude of the full magnetic-field vector, and not an
unsigned poloidal-field magnitude. It is the calibrated field value, not the
raw electrical signal, and is therefore distinct from the [voltage of a
poloidal magnetic-field
probe](name:voltage_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe); it is also distinct
from the linearly calibrated value before the nonlinear correction is
applied. Probe hardware descriptors such as the [turn count of a poloidal
magnetic-field probe](name:turn_count_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe)
characterize the sensor and are not components of the field.

This quantity is the probe-local, oriented-component counterpart of the
[poloidal magnetic field](name:poloidal_magnetic_field), evaluated at one
sensing position along one fixed sensitive direction rather than as a field
over the plasma domain.

Sign convention: Positive when the local magnetic-field vector at the probe
sensing position has a positive projection along the probe's positive
poloidal sensitive direction in the $R$-$Z$ plane of the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: height_of_toroidal_field_coil
items.description:
Full binormal extent of a rectangular toroidal-field-coil conductor
cross-section, measured across its external envelope in the local
Frenet–Serret frame.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the full dimension of a rectangular toroidal-field-coil
conductor cross-section along the binormal direction of its local
right-handed Frenet–Serret frame. The frame consists of tangent, normal, and
binormal unit vectors, with the binormal perpendicular to the conductor
centerline and the other two directions.

For opposing cross-section boundaries, the full binormal height is defined
by

$$
h_b = b_{\max} - b_{\min}
$$

where $b_{\max}$ and $b_{\min}$ are the extreme signed binormal coordinates
of the external cross-section envelope. The coordinate convention is
consistent with the [binormal coordinate of the toroidal field
coil](name:binormal_coordinate_of_toroidal_field_coil), which describes
individual outline vertices.

This is a gross geometric envelope dimension; it is not the net
current-carrying material thickness, insulation thickness, or a local signed
coordinate.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_conductor_cross_section
items.description:
Vertical coordinate of the geometric center of a rectangular conductor
cross-section in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Vertical coordinate of the geometric center of a rectangular conductor
cross-section in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where
$R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical position.

The coordinate is defined by

$$
Z = \mathbf{x}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is the position vector of the geometric center relative
to an origin on the toroidal symmetry axis in the chosen zero-height plane,
and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along that axis toward increasing
vertical position.

This is the [vertical coordinate of the rectangle
center](name:vertical_coordinate_of_rectangle_center) applied to a conductor
cross-section. It locates one cross-section center, not an average over
conductor elements, the rectangle's vertical extent, or an outline vertex.

Sign convention: Positive when the geometric center lies above the
zero-height plane in the direction of increasing $Z$.

items.name: tritium_breeding_ratio
items.description:
Tritium breeding ratio is the blanket-level ratio of tritium atoms produced
in breeder-blanket breeding regions to the incident fusion-neutron count
over the same normalization interval. Compatible module contributions share
this denominator and add to the blanket value.
items.documentation:
Tritium breeding ratio is the blanket-level ratio of tritium atoms produced
inside the breeding regions of a breeder blanket to the incident
fusion-neutron count used to normalize the same neutronics balance. It is a
tritium production figure of merit for the blanket as a whole, distinct from
nuclear heating or power deposition.

The ratio is defined over a specified normalization interval by

$$
\mathrm{TBR} = \frac{N_{T,\mathrm{blanket}}}{N_{n,\mathrm{inc}}}
$$

where $N_{T,\mathrm{blanket}}$ is the number of tritium atoms produced in
the blanket breeding regions during that interval, and $N_{n,\mathrm{inc}}$
is the incident fusion-neutron count for the same interval.

Breeding regions are the blanket material volumes designated for
neutron-induced tritium production; tritium produced outside those volumes
is excluded unless that material is part of the breeder blanket breeding
region. The denominator is the common incident-neutron denominator, not the
number of neutrons absorbed in the blanket and not a module-specific
denominator. Compatible non-overlapping module values of
[tritium_breeding_ratio_of_breeder_blanket_module](name:tritium_breeding_ratio_of_breeder_blanket_module)
that use this same denominator are additive and sum to the blanket-level
ratio.

The quantity differs from power_of_breeder_blanket and
[power_of_breeder_blanket_module](name:power_of_breeder_blanket_module),
which describe energy deposition rates rather than tritium atom yield.
Because both counts are non-negative and the denominator must be positive,
negative values are outside the physical domain; values greater than one
mean more tritium atoms are produced than the tritium atoms consumed by the
fusion reactions that generated the same incident-neutron population, which
is the breeding condition for tritium self-sufficiency.

items.name: mach_number
items.description:
Dimensionless vector ratio of plasma flow velocity to the local sound speed,
retaining directional components of the flow.
items.documentation:
The Mach-number vector is the plasma flow velocity normalized by the local
sound speed. Its magnitude expresses flow speed relative to sound speed,
while its directional components retain the signed flow projection. The
family includes directional quantities such as the [parallel Mach
number](name:parallel_mach_number).

$$
\mathbf{M} = \frac{\mathbf{v}}{c_s}
$$

where $\mathbf{M}$ is the Mach-number vector, $\mathbf{v}$ is the plasma
flow-velocity vector, and $c_s$ is the local sound speed. For a specified
direction $a$, the corresponding component is $M_a = v_a/c_s$, where $v_a$
is the flow-velocity projection along that direction.

The quantity is dimensionless and is distinct from the unnormalized flow
velocity; the sound-speed definition and the selected projection determine
the specific physical interpretation of each component.

items.name: average_temperature_over_scrape_off_layer
items.description:
Averaged kinetic temperature of a specified plasma species over the
open-field-line scrape-off layer, with the averaging domain and measure
defined by its specialization.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the temperature of a specified plasma species after
averaging over a defined domain or path within the scrape-off layer. The
scrape-off layer is the open-field-line region outside the last closed
magnetic flux surface.

The averaged temperature is defined by

$$
\overline{T}_s = \frac{\int_{\mathcal{D}} T_s\,d\mu}{\int_{\mathcal{D}} d\mu}
$$

where $\overline{T}_s$ is the averaged temperature, $T_s$ is the local
temperature of species $s$, $\mathcal{D}$ is the specified scrape-off-layer
domain or path, and $d\mu$ is the averaging measure. For [field-line-average
temperature over the scrape-off
layer](name:field_line_average_temperature_over_scrape_off_layer),
$\mathcal{D}$ is an open magnetic field line between its defined upstream
and downstream locations and $d\mu$ is the corresponding path measure.

The quantity is species-specific and does not sum temperatures over multiple
species or represent a local pointwise temperature. It is an averaged
specialization of [temperature over the scrape-off
layer](name:temperature_over_scrape_off_layer), while the concrete averaging
domain and measure distinguish each child quantity.

items.name: first_measurement_direction_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone
items.description:
Unit direction vector defining the first measurement direction associated
with an elliptic shatter cone in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the unit direction vector assigned to the first measurement
direction of an elliptic shatter cone. It describes orientation, not
position, length, or cone-axis magnitude. Its components are resolved in the
right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame, with
$\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$ representing the vertical direction.

$$
\hat{\mathbf{d}}_1 = d_{1x}\hat{x} + d_{1y}\hat{y} + d_{1z}\hat{z}, \qquad d_{1x}^2+d_{1y}^2+d_{1z}^2=1
$$

Here, $\hat{\mathbf{d}}_1$ is the first measurement-direction unit vector,
$d_{1x}$, $d_{1y}$, and $d_{1z}$ are its Cartesian projections, and
$\hat{x}$, $\hat{y}$, and $\hat{z}$ are the Cartesian basis vectors. The
designation “first” follows the shatter-cone measurement-direction
convention and does not imply alignment with the Cartesian $x$ axis. It is
distinct from the [X component of the shatter-cone major-axis unit
vector](name:x_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), which describes cone
geometry rather than measurement-direction ordering.

items.name: effective_charge_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Effective charge number of the ion mixture at the plasma boundary is the
charge-squared-weighted sum of ionic number densities divided by the
electron number density at that boundary. It equals one for a purely singly
charged hydrogenic ion mixture and increases with impurity charge content.
items.documentation:
Effective charge number of the ion mixture at the plasma boundary is the
charge-squared-weighted sum of ionic number densities divided by the
electron number density, evaluated at the plasma boundary where the confined
plasma meets the last closed flux surface. Because each ion population is
weighted by the square of its charge number, higher charge states contribute
disproportionately to this quantity relative to their particle density.

The boundary value is defined from the charge-state-resolved ion densities
by

$$
Z_{\mathrm{eff},b} = \frac{\sum_i n_{i,b} Z_i^2}{n_{e,b}}
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{eff},b}$ is the effective charge at the plasma boundary,
$i$ indexes every ion species and charge state present at the boundary,
$n_{i,b}$ is the number density of ion population $i$ at the boundary in
$\mathrm{m}^{-3}$, $Z_i$ is its charge number, and $n_{e,b}$ is the electron
number density at the boundary in $\mathrm{m}^{-3}$. Under quasineutrality,
$n_{e,b} = \sum_i n_{i,b} Z_i$, so the denominator equals the
charge-weighted (first-moment) sum of the same ion densities.

The sum includes all ion species and all charge states at the boundary; for
a quasineutral, purely singly charged hydrogenic ion mixture,
$Z_{\mathrm{eff},b} = 1$, and any admixture of multiply charged impurities
raises the value above unity. This local boundary value is distinct from
[flux-surface-averaged effective charge at the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_effective_charge_at_plasma_boundary),
which applies an explicit average over the boundary flux surface, and from
[effective charge at the limiter](name:effective_charge_at_limiter), which
is evaluated at the limiter contact location rather than at the plasma
boundary.

items.name: momentum_damping_rate
items.description:
Effective inverse relaxation time for loss of ordered fluid momentum through
collisional friction and neoclassical viscosity; the general structural
parent for species-, charge-state-, and projection-resolved momentum damping
rates.
items.documentation:
The momentum damping rate $\nu_D$ is the reciprocal relaxation time that
quantifies how rapidly ordered fluid momentum is dissipated within a plasma
population through inter-species collisional friction and neoclassical
viscous stresses. It enters the fluid momentum balance as a linear loss
coefficient applied to the local momentum density, capturing the collective
effect of Coulomb collisions and drift-driven viscosity acting on any
directed flow component.

The defining relation for a fluid momentum component $p$ subject to damping
is:

$$
\frac{\partial p}{\partial t}\bigg|_{\rm damp} = -\nu_D \, p
$$

where $\nu_D$ is the damping rate and $p$ is the local fluid momentum
density. The magnitude of $\nu_D$ depends on plasma collisionality, species
masses and charges, and the local magnetic geometry.

This name is the structural parent for species- and projection-resolved
variants. In transport models, $\nu_D$ is derived analytically from
neoclassical friction-force coefficients or from velocity-space integrals of
the collision operator evaluated at the local plasma parameters.
Ion-population values are provided by
[ion_momentum_damping_rate](name:ion_momentum_damping_rate);
charge-state-resolved counterparts are given by
[ion_state_momentum_damping_rate](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate).
Directional projections include poloidal_ion_state_momentum_damping_rate,
toroidal_ion_state_momentum_damping_rate,
parallel_ion_state_momentum_damping_rate, and
[radial_ion_state_momentum_damping_rate](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate).

items.name: ion_particle_flux
items.description:
Ion particle flux is the signed net number of ions of one species crossing
an oriented surface per unit area and time, summed over all ionic charge
states.
items.documentation:
Ion particle flux is the signed net number flow of ions of one specified
species through an oriented surface per unit area and time. It is the
surface-normal projection of ion number transport, without selecting a fixed
geometric or magnetic-field direction.

The local flux is defined by the normal velocity moment summed over ionic
charge states:

$$
\Gamma_i = \sum_q \int (\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}) f_{i,q}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $\Gamma_i$ is the ion particle flux, $i$ labels the specified ion
species, $q$ labels its ionic charge states, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle
velocity, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the chosen surface unit normal, $f_{i,q}$ is
the local velocity distribution of that species in charge state $q$, and
$d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The velocity integral of each
distribution is the corresponding charge-state number density.

The quantity includes thermal and nonthermal ions and is summed over all
ionic charge states of the specified species; neutral particles and other
ion species are excluded. It is a local net flux, not a one-way incident
flux or a surface-integrated particle rate. Particles are counted without
charge weighting, so this is not electric current density.

Each charge-state contribution is an [ion charge-state particle
flux](name:ion_charge_state_particle_flux); their sum gives this
species-level quantity. Unlike [ion energy flux](name:ion_energy_flux), it
counts transported particles rather than the energy they carry.

Sign convention: Positive when the net ion number flow crosses the surface
in the direction of the chosen unit normal.

items.name: toroidal_deuterium_tritium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Mass-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of the effective deuterium–tritium
fuel species evaluated at the magnetic axis.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the mass-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of
deuterium–tritium fuel treated as an effective single species at the
magnetic axis, the innermost point of nested closed poloidal magnetic-flux
surfaces. It represents collective fuel motion rather than speed or an
isotope-specific velocity.

The effective velocity is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,DT} = \frac{\rho_D v_{\phi,D} + \rho_T v_{\phi,T}}{\rho_D + \rho_T}
$$

where $\rho_D$ and $\rho_T$ are the deuterium and tritium mass densities,
and $v_{\phi,D}$ and $v_{\phi,T}$ are their toroidal bulk-flow velocities in
the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The isotope-specific
[toroidal tritium velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_tritium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) is therefore not
identical to this effective-species value. The quantity excludes poloidal
and radial velocity components and differs from the corresponding fuel
velocity at the [internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_deuterium_tritium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).

Sign convention: Positive when the effective deuterium–tritium bulk velocity
points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_pumping
items.description:
Rate at which particles of a specified neutral species are removed from the
plasma region by wall pumping, giving global neutral-particle exhaust
throughput.
items.documentation:
The rate at which particles of a specified neutral species are removed from
the plasma region by wall pumping is the global scalar representation of the
wall particle-removal flux. It describes pumped neutral-particle exhaust at
material surfaces due only to pumping.

The pumped neutral-particle flux is defined as the removal term in the
neutral-particle inventory balance:

$$
\Phi_{n,\mathrm{pump}} = -\left.\frac{dN_n}{dt}\right|_{\mathrm{pump}}
$$

where $\Phi_{n,\mathrm{pump}}$ is the neutral particle flux at the wall due
to pumping, $N_n$ is the total particle inventory of the specified neutral
species in the plasma region, and $t$ is time.

This quantity applies to one specified neutral species and is aggregated
globally over the wall pumping interface. It is not summed over different
neutral species and does not include ionized-particle exhaust, recycling or
sputtering sources, neutralization sources, or particle losses not
attributed to wall pumping.

This flux is the neutral-species member of the broader [particle flux at
wall due to pumping](name:particle_rate_at_wall_due_to_pumping) family and
is distinct from the [electron-equivalent particle flux at wall due to
pumping](name:electron_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_pumping). It is the
removal rate itself, not a pumping-speed or first-order loss coefficient; if
a model represents pumping by a coefficient $S_{n,\mathrm{pump}}$ acting on
$N_n$, then $\Phi_{n,\mathrm{pump}}$ is related to that model by
$\Phi_{n,\mathrm{pump}} = S_{n,\mathrm{pump}} N_n$, where
$S_{n,\mathrm{pump}}$ is the neutral-species pumping coefficient.

items.name: wave_mode_number
items.description:
Dimensionless mode-number vector labeling the discrete Fourier periodicities
of a coherent wave perturbation.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the collection of discrete mode labels that identifies a
coherent wave perturbation through its periodic phase dependence. It is a
mode-index vector, not a spatial wavevector, physical displacement vector,
or full linear-MHD eigenmode label.

For a coherent perturbation represented by a single Fourier phase in
periodic coordinates, the wave mode-number vector is defined by

$$
\tilde{q}(\boldsymbol{\alpha}, t) = \hat{q}\,\exp\!\left[i\left(\mathbf{N}_w \cdot \boldsymbol{\alpha} - \omega t\right)\right]
$$

where $\tilde{q}$ is the coherent wave perturbation of a field quantity,
$\hat{q}$ is its complex amplitude, $\boldsymbol{\alpha}$ is the set of
periodic coordinates used to label the phase, $\mathbf{N}_w$ is the wave
mode-number vector, and $\omega$ is the angular frequency.

This parent covers Fourier harmonic labels of coherent waves, such as the
[toroidal wave mode number](name:toroidal_wave_mode_number) associated with
toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.
It does not by itself assert a radial branch index or a poloidal harmonic;
those belong only to more specific quantities when explicitly defined, and
distinguish it from the broader linear-MHD mode number.

Sign convention: Positive when increasing the associated periodic coordinate
at fixed time increases the Fourier phase in the representation above.

items.name: total_runaway_electron_current
items.description:
Total runaway-electron current is the electric-current vector carried by the
runaway-electron population, defined component by component by integrating
the corresponding runaway-electron current-density component over a poloidal
cross-section. It represents conventional current, not runaway-electron
particle flux.
items.documentation:
Total runaway-electron current is the electric-current vector carried by the
runaway-electron population, defined component by component by integrating
the corresponding runaway-electron current-density component over a poloidal
cross-section. It is the conventional electric current associated with
runaway electrons, not the runaway-electron particle flux or momentum.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$ basis
associated with coordinates $(R,\phi,Z)$, with $R$ major radius, $\phi$
toroidal angle increasing counterclockwise viewed from the $+\hat{Z}$ side,
and $Z$ vertical height, the component definition is:

$$
I_{\mathrm{RE},a} = \int_{S_p} j_{\mathrm{RE},a}\, dA,\qquad a\in\{R,\phi,Z\}
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{RE},a}$ is the component of the total runaway-electron
current, $j_{\mathrm{RE},a}$ is the corresponding component of the
runaway-electron current-density vector, $S_p$ is a poloidal cross-section
at fixed toroidal angle $\phi$, and $dA$ is its area element.

This quantity denotes the component-general vector, not only the toroidal
projection. The [toroidal total runaway-electron
current](name:toroidal_total_runaway_electron_current) is the $\hat{\phi}$
component specialization obtained by the same cross-sectional component
integral in the right-handed cylindrical $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$
basis.

Sign convention: Positive when a component is aligned with the corresponding
positive basis vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi},
\hat{Z})$ basis; the toroidal component is positive for conventional current
in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential
items.description:
Vector-potential perturbation associated with a change in the plasma
magnetic field relative to a reference state, retaining radial, poloidal,
and toroidal components.
items.documentation:
The perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential is the vector-valued
departure of the plasma magnetic vector potential from its reference state.
Its curl determines the associated perturbed magnetic field, subject to the
chosen vector-potential gage.

The perturbation is defined by

$$
\delta \mathbf{A} = \mathbf{A} - \mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{ref}}
$$

where $\delta \mathbf{A}$ is the perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential,
$\mathbf{A}$ is the plasma magnetic vector potential, and
$\mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is its reference-state value. The associated
magnetic-field perturbation satisfies $\delta \mathbf{B} = \nabla \times
\delta \mathbf{A}$, where $\delta \mathbf{B}$ is the perturbed magnetic
field and $\nabla$ is the spatial differential operator.

This quantity denotes the complete perturbation vector in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It includes the radial,
poloidal, and toroidal components without summing their signed projections.
The [radial perturbed plasma magnetic vector
potential](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential),
[poloidal perturbed plasma magnetic vector
potential](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential), and
[toroidal perturbed plasma magnetic vector
potential](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential) are
component-specific instances of this vector quantity.

The perturbation excludes the reference-state contribution and is distinct
from the full [plasma magnetic vector
potential](name:plasma_magnetic_vector_potential), which includes both
reference and perturbed parts. Because a vector potential is gage-dependent,
only its curl determines the corresponding magnetic-field perturbation
uniquely.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved component of $\delta \mathbf{A}$
points along its defined positive radial, poloidal, or toroidal direction in
the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description:
Flux limiter coefficient is a multiplicative factor, or vector of factors,
that scales a collisionless free-streaming bound on a flux density while
preserving the direction or sign of each resolved flux component.
items.documentation:
Flux limiter coefficient is a multiplicative factor, or vector of factors,
that scales a collisionless free-streaming upper bound on a flux density in
a transport closure. It limits the magnitude permitted by that bound while
preserving the direction or sign assigned to each resolved flux component by
the underlying closure.

For a resolved flux-density component indexed by $i$, a direction-preserving
limited flux can be expressed as:

$$
F_i = \operatorname{sgn}\!\left(F_i^{\mathrm{cl}}\right)\min\!\left(\left|F_i^{\mathrm{cl}}\right|, L_i F_i^{\mathrm{fs}}\right)
$$

where $F_i$ is the limited flux-density component, $F_i^{\mathrm{cl}}$ is
the unconstrained closure value, $F_i^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the corresponding
collisionless free-streaming bound, and $L_i$ is the flux limiter
coefficient for that component. The limiting range is typically $0 \le L_i
\le 1$, with smaller values imposing a stricter cap.

This parent quantity does not specify the transported quantity, resolved
component, or spatial region. It covers both generic region-scoped flux
limiting, such as the edge-region flux limiter coefficient, and
quantity-specific limiting, such as the [momentum-flux limiter
coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient); child names identify
any additional component or region semantics.

items.name: poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part
items.description:
The imaginary part of the complex poloidal component of the first-order
perturbed plasma magnetic-field eigenfunction for a single toroidal Fourier
mode in linear MHD stability analysis.
items.documentation:
The imaginary part of the complex poloidal component of the first-order
perturbed plasma magnetic-field eigenfunction for a single toroidal Fourier
mode in linear MHD stability analysis is the coefficient of $+i$ in the
poloidal projection of that eigenfunction. The projection is onto $\hat
e_\theta$, the local unit direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in
the flux-coordinate system $(s,\theta,\phi)$, where $s$ is a radial
flux-surface label and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame with $R$ major radius, $Z$ vertical height,
and $\phi$ increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat Z$.

For the normal-mode representation with toroidal Fourier factor
$\exp[i(n\phi-\omega t)]$, the defining relation is:

$$
B_{\theta,\mathrm{Im}}(s,\theta) = \operatorname{Im}\!\left\{\tilde{\mathbf{B}}(s,\theta)\cdot\hat e_\theta\right\}
$$

where $B_{\theta,\mathrm{Im}}$ is this quantity, $\tilde{\mathbf{B}}$ is the
complex first-order perturbed plasma magnetic-field eigenfunction,
$\operatorname{Im}$ extracts the coefficient multiplying $+i$, and $i$ is
the imaginary unit. The projection $\tilde{\mathbf{B}}\cdot\hat e_\theta$
and $B_{\theta,\mathrm{Im}}$ have unit T; $n$, $\omega$, and $t$ are the
integer toroidal mode number, complex angular eigenfrequency, and time,
respectively.

This quantity applies to the perturbed magnetic field in the plasma region
and excludes the corresponding [poloidal perturbed vacuum magnetic field
imaginary
part](name:poloidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part). It is
the imaginary counterpart of [poloidal perturbed plasma magnetic field real
part](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part) and, together
with that real part, specifies the complex [poloidal perturbed plasma
magnetic field](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field) for the
chosen eigenfunction normalization and overall complex phase; changing that
phase rotates the real and imaginary parts without changing the physical
mode.

Sign convention: Positive when the coefficient multiplying $+i$ in the
projection of the complex eigenfunction onto the local $+\hat e_\theta$
direction is positive for the Fourier factor $\exp[i(n\phi-\omega t)]$.

items.name: x_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone
items.description:
Signed x projection of the unit vector along an elliptic shatter cone’s
minor geometric axis in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the signed projection of the unit vector directed along the
minor geometric axis of an elliptic shatter cone onto the Cartesian x
direction. It specifies one orientation coordinate of that hardware axis.

Let $u_x$ denote this x component, $\hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\mathrm{minor}}$ the
unit vector along the shatter cone’s minor axis, and $\hat{\mathbf{x}}$ the
unit vector toward increasing x in the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$
frame. The defining projection is

$$
u_x = \hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\mathrm{minor}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{x}}
$$

The component is bounded between −1 and 1 because
$\hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\mathrm{minor}}$ is normalized.

This quantity applies only to the minor axis of the shatter cone and
represents one Cartesian component; it is neither the complete direction
vector, its magnitude, nor an aggregation over axes or hardware objects. It
is distinct from the corresponding [x component of the major-axis unit
vector](name:x_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone).

Together with the other Cartesian components of the same minor-axis unit
vector, including the [z component of the minor-axis unit
vector](name:z_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), this component
specifies the minor-axis orientation.

items.name: curvature_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
items.description:
Radius of curvature of an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror along a
selected first or second local tangential direction, characterizing
directional surface bending relevant to reflected-beam focusing or
defocusing.
items.documentation:
Directional radius of curvature is the length scale of bending of the
electron-cyclotron launcher mirror surface in a selected mirror-local
tangential direction. It characterizes the direction-dependent geometric
contribution of the mirror surface to reflected-beam focusing or defocusing.

For direction $i$, the radius is the reciprocal of the magnitude of the
surface's normal curvature in that direction:

$$
R_i = \frac{1}{|\kappa_i|}
$$

where $R_i$ is the radius of curvature, $\kappa_i$ is the normal curvature
of the mirror surface in the normal section tangent to direction $i$, and
$i$ identifies the selected first or second local tangential direction. A
planar direction has zero normal curvature and an unbounded radius.

The selected direction is the [first local tangential
direction](name:first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror)
or the [second local tangential
direction](name:second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror).
The radius applies only when curvature is specified in that direction:
curvature types 2, 4, or 5 for the first direction, and types 3 or 5 for the
second. It is directional, not an average over the two directions.

The corresponding [first local tangential
width](name:first_local_tangential_width_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror)
and [second local tangential
width](name:second_local_tangential_width_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror)
describe surface extent rather than bending. This mirror-surface radius is
distinct from the [wave curvature of an electron-cyclotron
beam](name:wave_curvature_of_electron_cyclotron_beam), which describes the
beam's phase-front curvature.

items.name: electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface
items.description:
Cumulative wave power absorbed by all electron populations, thermal and
fast, from a specified wave source or source set within the plasma volume
enclosed by a magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
The electron power at inside flux surface is the cumulative rate at which
wave energy from a specified source or source set is deposited into the
electron population, spanning both thermal bulk electrons and fast
suprathermal electrons, within the plasma volume bounded by a closed
magnetic flux surface. It is an enclosed-volume channel quantity: each
bounding surface includes all electron wave absorption inside that surface.

For a local volumetric electron wave-power deposition density, the
cumulative power is

$$
P_e(\psi_s) = \int_{V(\psi_s)} p_e^{\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $P_e(\psi_s)$ is this cumulative electron wave power, $\psi_s$ is the
magnetic-flux-surface label of the bounding surface, $V(\psi_s)$ is the
plasma volume enclosed by that surface, $p_e^{\mathrm{wave}}$ is the local
volumetric rate of wave energy deposition into the electron population,
$\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is the volume element.

For the same wave channel and enclosed volume, this quantity satisfies the
population decomposition $P_e = P_{e,\mathrm{thermal}} +
P_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$, with components [thermal electron power at inside flux
surface](name:thermal_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface) and [fast
electron power at inside flux
surface](name:fast_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface). It is the
electron counterpart of [ion power at inside flux
surface](name:ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface) and a species-specific
instance of [power at inside flux
surface](name:power_at_inside_flux_surface); it excludes ion absorption and
non-wave loss or exchange channels.

Sign convention: Positive when wave energy is deposited into the electron
population.

items.name: equilibrium_weight_of_interferometer_beam
items.description:
Dimensionless factor controlling the relative contribution of an
interferometer beam’s line-integrated electron-density residual to an
equilibrium objective function.
items.documentation:
The equilibrium weight assigned to an interferometer-beam constraint is a
nonnegative factor that sets the relative importance of its line-integrated
electron-density residual in an equilibrium objective function. It applies
to the constraint associated with one interferometer beam rather than to the
electron density itself.

A weighted least-squares objective containing this constraint is defined by

$$
J = \frac{1}{2} \sum_i w_i^2 \left(\frac{y_i^{\mathrm{rec}} - y_i^{\mathrm{meas}}}{\sigma_i}\right)^2
$$

where $J$ is the equilibrium objective function, $i$ indexes individual
constraints, $w_i$ is the equilibrium weight, $y_i^{\mathrm{rec}}$ is the
reconstructed line-integrated electron density for constraint $i$,
$y_i^{\mathrm{meas}}$ is its measured line-integrated electron density, and
$\sigma_i$ is the standard deviation assigned to its measurement error.

For this quantity, $i$ denotes an interferometer-beam line-integrated
electron-density constraint. The weight is specific to that individual
constraint; the objective function aggregates all constraint contributions
through the summation. It is not the line-integrated electron density,
either its measured or reconstructed value, and it is distinct from the
[calibration coefficient of an interferometer
beam](name:spectral_calibration_factor_at_line_of_sight), which
characterizes signal calibration rather than equilibrium-objective
weighting.

This quantity has the same objective-function role as the equilibrium weight
of a flux loop and the equilibrium weight of a poloidal magnetic-field
probe; those related weights differ by the physical measurement constraint
to which they apply.

items.name: line_averaged_helium_3_density
items.description:
Line-averaged helium-3 density is the chord-length average of local ionized
helium-3 density along a specified viewing path, excluding neutral atoms.
items.documentation:
Line-averaged helium-3 density is the chord-length average of the local
helium-3 ion number density along a specified path. It includes singly
ionized $^3\mathrm{He}^{+}$ and fully stripped $^3\mathrm{He}^{2+}$ ions,
while excluding neutral helium-3 atoms.

The line average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_{^3\mathrm{He}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_{0}^{L} n_{^3\mathrm{He}}(s)\,\mathrm{d}s
$$

where $\overline{n}_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ is the line-averaged density,
$n_{^3\mathrm{He}}(s)$ is the local charge-state-summed density at path
coordinate $s$, and $L$ is the chord length. Unlike the volume average in
[volume-averaged helium-3 density](name:volume_averaged_helium_3_density),
this quantity weights each position uniformly by distance along the path. It
is a path-integrated representation of [helium-3
density](name:helium_3_density), not a separate charge-state population.

items.name: width_of_passive_structure
items.description:
Full radial extent of a rectangular passive conducting structure element in
the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The radial width is the full major-radius extent of a rectangular passive
conducting structure element, measured between its inner and outer radial
boundaries.

$$
W = R_{\mathrm{outer}} - R_{\mathrm{inner}}
$$

where $W$ is the radial width, and $R_{\mathrm{outer}}$ and
$R_{\mathrm{inner}}$ are the major-radius coordinates in meters of the outer
and inner boundaries in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The quantity is non-negative and describes radial extent only; it is
distinct from the full vertical extent given by [height of passive
structure](name:height_of_passive_structure) and from the element length
given by length of passive structure.

items.name: iron_density_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Local number density of iron ions, summed over all ionization states,
evaluated at the core-side top of the H-mode edge pedestal.
items.documentation:
Iron-ion number density is the local amount of ionized iron per unit plasma
volume at the H-mode edge-pedestal top.

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Fe}} = \sum_{q=1}^{Z_{\mathrm{Fe}}} n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the total iron-ion number density,
$n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}$ is the number density of iron ions in charge state
$q$, $q$ is the positive ionization-state index, and $Z_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is
the atomic number of iron and maximum positive charge state. The quantity is
evaluated at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge pedestal, whose
position is defined by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal).

The aggregation includes all positive iron ionization states and excludes
neutral iron and ions of every other element. It is therefore distinct from
a charge-state-resolved iron-ion density and from the total density of all
ion species.

This density is an additive species contribution to the total ion density at
the same location and provides one of the density weights entering the [ion
average temperature at the pedestal
top](name:ion_average_temperature_at_pedestal_top).

items.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_neon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
items.description:
Dimensionless elemental abundance ratio of charge-state-summed neon nuclei
to free electrons, formed from their respective mean number densities inside
the last closed flux surface.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the abundance of neon nuclei relative to free electrons,
with both species represented by number densities averaged over the plasma
volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface. Neon is summed over all
charge states, so the quantity is an elemental composition ratio rather than
a charge-state-specific abundance or a local density ratio.

The ratio of volume-averaged densities is defined by

$$
\frac{\overline{n}_{\mathrm{Ne}}}{\overline{n}_e} = \frac{\displaystyle \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_{\mathrm{Ne}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV}{\displaystyle \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_e(\mathbf{x})\,dV}
$$

where $\overline{n}_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the [volume-averaged neon
density](name:volume_averaged_neon_density), $\overline{n}_e$ is the
[volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density),
$n_{\mathrm{Ne}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local neon nuclear number density
summed over charge states, $n_e(\mathbf{x})$ is the local free-electron
number density, $V_p$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux
surface, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $dV$ is the volume element.

Both operands use the same plasma volume and the same volume-averaging
convention. This quantity is the ratio of the two global means, not the
volume average of the local ratio
$n_{\mathrm{Ne}}(\mathbf{x})/n_e(\mathbf{x})$; its denominator is
specifically the parent [volume-averaged electron
density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), while its numerator is the
corresponding [volume-averaged neon
density](name:volume_averaged_neon_density).

items.name: wave_current_amplitude_of_antenna_strap
items.description:
Peak magnitude of the radio-frequency current at a specified position along
an ion-cyclotron-heating antenna strap.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the peak magnitude of the radio-frequency current on an
ion-cyclotron-heating antenna strap at a specified position. It
characterizes the local electromagnetic excitation of a strap fed through a
single transmission line.

The amplitude $I_{\mathrm{amp}}$ is defined from the local RF current
waveform $i_{\mathrm{RF}}(t)$ by

$$
I_{\mathrm{amp}} = \max_t \left|i_{\mathrm{RF}}(t)\right|
$$

where $i_{\mathrm{RF}}(t)$ is the instantaneous radio-frequency current at
the specified strap position and $t$ is time.

The quantity applies locally along the antenna strap and represents the RF
wave-current amplitude, not a current summed over the antenna system or over
multiple straps. It is a non-negative magnitude and is distinct from the
signed instantaneous current and from an RMS current measure.

It is the amplitude transformation of the [wave current of an antenna
strap](name:wave_current_of_antenna_strap): the parent denotes the
oscillating current, whereas this quantity retains its peak magnitude at the
specified position.

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_conductor_cross_section
items.description:
Major-radius coordinate of a conductor cross-section's geometric center,
equal to its perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis.
items.documentation:
Major-radius coordinate of conductor cross section

It is the [major-radius coordinate](name:radial_coordinate) specialized to
this locus:

$$
R = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}
$$

where $x$ and $y$ are the Cartesian coordinates of that center in the
right-handed $(x, y, z)$ frame, with $z$ the vertical coordinate and the
origin on the toroidal symmetry axis.

The quantity applies individually to conductor cross-sections represented as
rectangles, without averaging over conductors. It specifies the center
position, not a cross-sectional width or an outline-point coordinate.

items.name: fast_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface
items.description:
Cumulative wave power absorbed by the fast (suprathermal) electron
population within the plasma volume enclosed by a specified magnetic flux
surface.
items.documentation:
Fast electron power at an inside flux surface quantifies the total rate at
which coherent wave energy is absorbed by the non-thermal fast electron
population within the plasma volume bounded by a given magnetic flux
surface. It is the fast-electron contribution to [electron power at an
inside flux surface](name:electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface), distinct
from the bulk thermal-electron contribution [thermal electron power at an
inside flux surface](name:thermal_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface).

The quantity is obtained by integrating the flux-surface-averaged [fast
electron power density](name:fast_electron_absorbed_wave_power_density)
$p_{\mathrm{fast,e}}$ over the enclosed plasma volume:

$$
P_{\mathrm{fast,e}}(\rho) = \int_0^\rho p_{\mathrm{fast,e}}(\rho') \frac{dV}{d\rho'} \, d\rho'
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{fast,e}}(\rho)$ is the cumulative absorbed power, $\rho$
labels the limiting flux surface, $\rho'$ is the integration variable,
$p_{\mathrm{fast,e}}$ is the local fast-electron absorbed power density, and
$dV/d\rho'$ is the differential enclosed volume per unit flux-surface label.
Only absorption by fast electrons is included; thermal-electron and ion
absorption, launched power, and power absorbed outside the enclosed volume
are excluded. At the outermost closed flux surface, the quantity gives the
total wave power absorbed by fast electrons.

items.name: parallel_ion_particle_flux
items.description:
Parallel ion particle flux is the signed net number flow of one ion species
along the local magnetic field per unit perpendicular area and time, summed
over all ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
Parallel ion particle flux is the local net transport of particles of one
ion species along the magnetic field, expressed per unit area perpendicular
to that field.

The parallel particle flux $\Gamma_{i,\parallel}$ of ion species $i$ is
defined by

$$
\Gamma_{i,\parallel} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}} = \sum_{q\geq 1} \Gamma_{iq,\parallel}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i$ is the species' total particle-flux vector,
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field, $q$ is
the positive ionic charge number, and $\Gamma_{iq,\parallel}$ is the
[parallel ion charge-state particle
flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_particle_flux) for species $i$ in
charge state $q$.

The quantity is summed over all ionic charge states of the selected species,
excluding its neutral form and other ion species. It counts net particle
transport rather than incoming particles alone and is neither a
surface-integrated particle rate nor the charge-weighted [parallel ion
current density](name:parallel_ion_current_density).

It specializes [ion particle flux](name:ion_particle_flux) by choosing the
oriented surface normal along the local magnetic field. Its reference area
is therefore perpendicular to the field, not the area of an arbitrarily
inclined material surface.

Sign convention: Positive when the net ion number flow is co-directed with
the local magnetic field.

items.name: parallel_total_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description:
Effective field-parallel advection coefficient for transport of aggregate
ion momentum in the edge plasma, distinct from the ion bulk-flow velocity.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective coefficient describing advective,
non-diffusive transport of aggregate ion [momentum](name:momentum) along the
local magnetic field in the edge plasma. It is a transport-closure
coefficient, not the ion bulk-flow velocity.

For a selected transported momentum component, the convective flux
satisfies:

$$
\Pi_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}} = V_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}} g_i
$$

where $\Pi_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the field-parallel convective
flux of that ion momentum component, $V_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is
this effective convection coefficient, and $g_i$ is the corresponding
aggregate ion momentum density. The subscript $i$ identifies the ion
population. The parallel direction follows $\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf
B/|\mathbf B|$, where $\mathbf B$ is the local magnetic field and
$\hat{\mathbf b}$ is its direction unit vector.

The transported momentum density is summed over the included ion species and
their ionic charge states; electron and neutral momentum are excluded. The
coefficient acts on this aggregate momentum density and is not a sum of
charge-state convection velocities. The parallel qualification specifies the
transport direction, not an additional restriction on the transported
momentum component.

This quantity is the field-parallel projection of [ion momentum convection
velocity](name:ion_momentum_convection_velocity). Unlike [total momentum
convection velocity](name:total_momentum_convection_velocity), it applies
specifically to ion momentum rather than total plasma momentum. It is
distinct from [momentum diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity): the
convective coefficient multiplies momentum density, whereas the diffusive
coefficient multiplies its negative gradient.

Sign convention: Positive when effective momentum convection is along the
local magnetic-field direction.

items.name: neutron_flux_of_neutron_detector
items.description:
Fusion-neutron number flux incident on the neutron detector’s active
surface, giving the rate at which neutrons cross each unit of that surface.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the incident fusion-neutron number flux on the
neutron-sensitive active surface of the detector. It is the surface-crossing
flux, not the neutron production rate or the registered detection-event rate
described by rate of neutron detector. The parent quantity flux of neutron
detector expresses the same surface-transport concept.

The defining relation is

$$
\Phi_n = \frac{dN_n}{dA\,dt}
$$

where $\Phi_n$ is the incident neutron number flux, $N_n$ is the number of
neutrons crossing the active surface, $A$ is active surface area, and $t$ is
time. The surface is the neutron-sensitive area characterized by area of
neutron detector; passive housing, shielding, supports, and electronics are
excluded. Registered event rates additionally depend on detector response
and efficiency.

items.name: fast_current_density
items.description:
Fast-particle current density is the signed conventional electric-charge
flux per unit area carried by fast particles and resolved by magnetic-orbit
class.
items.documentation:
Fast-particle current density is the signed conventional charge-flux density
carried by fast particles. It is an orbit-resolved contribution to [current
density](name:current_density), with passing and trapped populations
represented as distinct contributions.

The kinetic definition is the charge-weighted first velocity moment
restricted to a selected magnetic-orbit class:

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{fast},\mathcal{O}}(\mathbf{x},t)=\sum_{s\in\mathrm{fast}}q_s\int_{\mathcal{O}}\mathbf{v}\,f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $t$ is time, $s$ indexes included
fast-particle species, $q_s$ is particle charge, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle
velocity, $f_s$ is the velocity-space distribution function, and
$\mathcal{O}$ is the selected orbit class.

The orbit class may be co-passing, counter-passing, or trapped, as
represented by [co-passing fast current
density](name:co_passing_fast_current_density), [counter-passing fast
current density](name:counter_passing_fast_current_density), and [trapped
fast current density](name:trapped_fast_current_density). Compensating
electron and thermal-ion return-current contributions are excluded from the
fast-particle contribution; they belong to other components of the total
current density.

Sign convention: Positive when the selected scalar projection of the
fast-particle charge flux is aligned with the positive direction defining
that projection.

items.name: incident_neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
items.description:
Incident number flux density of neutral recombination products arriving at a
plasma-facing wall, summed over neutral species and internal states.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the incoming neutral-particle count flux at a wall
attributable to recombination, with neutral product species and internal
states aggregated. It selects particles arriving at the surface, rather than
neutral particles emitted from it.

The incident flux density is defined from the recombination-attributed
neutral distribution by

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{inc}}^{\mathrm{rec}}(\mathbf{x}_w)=\int_{\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}<0} \left|\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}\right| f_{\mathrm{n,rec}}(\mathbf{x}_w,\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $\mathbf{x}_w$ is the wall position, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the outward
wall normal, $\mathbf{v}$ is neutral-particle velocity, and
$f_{\mathrm{n,rec}}$ is the recombination-attributed neutral distribution
summed over species and internal states.

This incident quantity is distinct from the outgoing emission described by
[neutral particle flux at the wall due to
recombination](name:neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination). A
state-resolved counterpart, [incident neutral internal-state particle flux
at the wall due to
recombination](name:incident_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination),
retains the internal-state distinction.

items.name: first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_reflector
items.description:
Signed first local-tangential coordinate of a reflector-outline vertex in
the reflector's orthogonal local frame (X1, X2), supplying one coordinate of
its irregular polygonal boundary.
items.documentation:
This quantity gives the position of an individual reflector-outline vertex
projected onto the first axis of the reflector-local orthogonal frame $(X_1,
X_2)$. Together with the corresponding second-axis coordinate, it specifies
the vertex locations that define the reflector's irregular polygonal
outline.

For vertex $i$, the coordinate is defined by

$$
x_{1,i} = \mathbf{r}_i \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_1
$$

where $\mathbf{r}_i$ is the vertex displacement from the reflector's local
origin and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1$ is the unit vector along the first local
tangential axis. The analogous coordinate for another object is defined by
the [first local-tangential coordinate of an optical
element](name:first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_optical_element).

This quantity describes reflector-outline geometry only; it is not the
reflector center, surface curvature, or an optical-path coordinate.

items.name: toroidal_wave_vector_of_beam_tracing_beam
items.description:
Signed toroidal projection of the local electromagnetic wave vector on a
beam-tracing beam, specifying spatial phase variation around the toroidal
symmetry axis.
items.documentation:
The toroidal wave-vector component is the signed projection of an
electromagnetic wave’s local spatial phase gradient onto the toroidal
direction, evaluated on the beam-tracing beam.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the component is defined
by

$$
k_\phi = \mathbf{k}\cdot\hat{\phi} = \frac{1}{R}\frac{\partial S}{\partial\phi}
$$

where $k_\phi$ is the toroidal wave-vector component, $\mathbf{k}$ is the
local [wave vector](name:wave_vector), $S$ is the spatial wave phase, and
$\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector toward increasing toroidal angle. Here $R$
is major radius measured from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is the [toroidal
angle at the beam-tracing
point](name:toroidal_coordinate_at_beam_tracing_point), increasing
counter-clockwise when viewed from above, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity applies locally along the beam, including at its launch point
when specifying the launched wave; it is not averaged along the propagation
path. It retains the magnitude dependence of the wave vector, unlike the
[normalized toroidal
component](name:normalized_toroidal_wave_vector_of_beam_tracing_beam), which
equals $k_\phi/|\mathbf{k}|$, where $|\mathbf{k}|$ is the wave-vector
magnitude.

Sign convention: Positive when the local wave vector has a projection toward
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: minor_length_of_passive_loop_element
items.description:
Length of the minor, beta-inclined side of a parallelogram-shaped
cross-section in a passive conductor element.
items.documentation:
The beta-inclined side length is the geometric length of a
parallelogram-shaped cross-section of a passive conductor element.

For the endpoints of the beta side, the length is defined by

$$
\ell_{\beta} = \left\|\mathbf{r}_{\beta,2} - \mathbf{r}_{\beta,1}\right\|
$$

where $\ell_{\beta}$ is the beta-side length, $\mathbf{r}_{\beta,1}$ and
$\mathbf{r}_{\beta,2}$ are the position vectors of its two endpoints, and
the norm is the Euclidean distance between those endpoints.

This quantity applies to one passive-loop conductor element and to its
minor, beta-inclined side only; it is not an aggregate over multiple
elements, the alpha-inclined major side, or the cross-sectional thickness.
The beta-side convention identifies this dimension as the minor counterpart
of the alpha-side dimension.

It is the minor-side component of the broader [length of a passive loop
element](name:length_of_passive_loop_element), which covers either inclined
side. The corresponding major-side quantity is the [major length of a
passive loop element](name:major_length_of_passive_loop_element); the two
side lengths describe distinct directions of the same oblique cross-section.

items.name: tritium_breeding_ratio_of_breeder_blanket_module
items.description:
Dimensionless tritium-production contribution from one breeder-blanket
module, normalized by the common incident fusion-neutron count used for the
blanket balance.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the contribution of one breeder-blanket module to the
blanket-level [tritium breeding ratio](name:tritium_breeding_ratio). It
counts tritium atoms produced within that module's breeding regions and uses
the common incident fusion-neutron normalization for the complete blanket.

$$
TBR_{\mathrm{module}} = \frac{N_{T,\mathrm{module}}}{N_{n,\mathrm{incident}}}
$$

where $N_{T,\mathrm{module}}$ is the number of tritium atoms produced in the
module's breeding regions and $N_{n,\mathrm{incident}}$ is the incident
fusion-neutron count used for the blanket balance.

For modules that partition the blanket breeding regions and share this
denominator, the module contributions add to the blanket tritium breeding
ratio. The quantity excludes tritium production outside the specified module
and is not a separate normalization of the module's incident neutron count.

items.name: ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Collisional torque density is the signed rate of angular-momentum transfer
per unit volume to a specified plasma population.
items.documentation:
Collisional torque density is the signed angular-momentum transfer rate per
unit volume delivered to a recipient plasma population by collisions. The
quantity applies across species-resolved forms, including [fast-ion
