collisional torque density](name:fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
and [thermal-ion collisional torque
density](name:thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions), within the
shared context of [collisional torque
density](name:torque_density_due_to_collisions).

The defining relation is

$$
\tau_{\mathrm{coll}} = \left.\frac{\partial \ell}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\tau_{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional torque density and $\ell$ is
the corresponding angular-momentum density of the recipient population. The
definition excludes torque from noncollisional forces and does not prescribe
a species, orbit class, or directional projection.

Sign convention: Positive when collisions transfer angular momentum into the
recipient population.

items.name: xenon_density
items.description:
Number density of xenon ions at a given point in the plasma, summed over all
ionization states from singly ionized through fully stripped xenon,
excluding neutral xenon atoms.
items.documentation:
Xenon is a high-$Z$ noble-gas impurity (atomic number $Z_\mathrm{Xe} = 54$)
introduced into fusion plasmas for radiative-mantle experiments,
impurity-transport studies, and disruption mitigation. The xenon ion number
density $n_\mathrm{Xe}$ quantifies the local concentration of all charged
xenon species and enters the plasma effective charge through $Z_\mathrm{eff}
= \sum_i Z_i^2 n_i / n_e$, where $n_i$ is the partial density of ion species
$i$ and $n_e$ is the electron density.

The total xenon ion density is the sum over all ionic charge states:

$$
n_\mathrm{Xe} = \sum_{z=1}^{54} n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{z+}}$ is the partial number density of xenon ions
carrying charge $ze$. The charge-state distribution is determined by coronal
equilibrium or collisional-radiative modeling at the local electron
temperature and density.

The xenon density profile is inferred from vacuum-ultraviolet or soft-X-ray
line emission via spectroscopy and tomographic inversion, or from
charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy using neutral-beam injection.
Spatially resolved forms include
[xenon_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:xenon_density_at_magnetic_axis) at the
innermost flux surface and xenon_density_at_pedestal in the edge transport
barrier, while
[volume_averaged_xenon_density](name:volume_averaged_xenon_density) provides
the global impurity content figure of merit. The dimensionless impurity
fraction relative to electron density is given by xenon_fraction.

items.name: effective_turn_count_of_passive_loop
items.description:
Effective turn count of a passive loop is the signed number of equivalent
windings assigned to a passive conducting loop for electromagnetic coupling.
It weights the passive-loop current contribution and may be fractional for
equivalent or homogenized loop elements.
items.documentation:
Effective turn count of a passive loop is the signed number of equivalent
windings assigned to a passive conducting loop for electromagnetic coupling.
It may be fractional when the represented conductor is an equivalent or
homogenized passive-loop element rather than a literal winding.

The signed current-turn source strength represented by the passive loop is
defined by:

$$
\mathcal{I}_{\mathrm{loop}} = N_{\mathrm{eff}} I_{\mathrm{loop}}
$$

where $\mathcal{I}_{\mathrm{loop}}$ is the signed current-turn source
strength of the passive loop, $N_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the effective turn count
of the passive loop, and $I_{\mathrm{loop}}$ is the [current of the passive
loop](name:current_of_passive_loop).

This quantity applies to the represented passive loop or passive-loop
element as one electromagnetic circuit contribution. It has no implicit
aggregation over multiple passive loops; if several represented windings or
conductor pieces are collapsed into one loop element, their net orientation
and coupling are represented by the single algebraic value of
$N_{\mathrm{eff}}$.

It is distinct from the [current of the passive
loop](name:current_of_passive_loop), which is multiplied by
$N_{\mathrm{eff}}$, and from the [area of the passive
loop](name:area_of_passive_loop), which describes conductor cross section.
It is not a turn count for magnetic probes, coil conductor elements,
toroidal-field coils, or magnetic field-line winding.

items.name: toroidal_angle_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe
items.description:
Signed azimuthal orientation angle of a poloidal magnetic-field probe’s
sensitive-axis normal in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the signed toroidal orientation of the sensitive-axis
normal of a poloidal magnetic-field probe coil. It measures the normal’s
departure from the poloidal plane through the orientation of its horizontal
projection.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the angle is defined by

$$
\alpha_{\mathrm{tor}} = \operatorname{atan2}(n_\phi,n_R), \qquad n_R=\mathbf{n}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{R}}, \quad n_\phi=\mathbf{n}\cdot\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\alpha_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal orientation angle,
$\mathbf{n}$ is the probe’s sensitive-axis unit normal, $n_R$ and $n_\phi$
are its cylindrical radial and toroidal components, and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$
and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ are the radial and toroidal unit vectors. Here
$R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height;
$\operatorname{atan2}$ returns the signed angle from the positive radial
direction to the horizontal projection of $\mathbf{n}$.

The quantity applies to the geometric orientation of each poloidal
magnetic-field probe coil. It is not the local plasma magnetic field, a
field component, or an angle averaged over probes, turns, or field samples.
The angle determines how the probe’s sensitive direction is related to the
local magnetic-field vector and therefore how the measured component is
projected. The corresponding toroidal orientation for a toroidal probe is
defined by
[toroidal_angle_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe](name:toroidal_angle_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe),
while its independent poloidal tilt is represented by
[poloidal_angle_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe](name:poloidal_angle_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe).

Sign convention: Positive when rotation from the positive radial direction
toward the horizontal projection of the sensitive-axis normal is toward
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: electrostatic_potential_real_part
items.description:
Electrostatic potential real part is the real-valued quadrature of a complex
electrostatic-potential representation. It identifies the in-phase
scalar-potential component, not the full complex potential or its magnitude.
items.documentation:
Electrostatic potential real part is the real-valued quadrature of a complex
electrostatic-potential field or eigenfunction. It represents the
scalar-potential component associated with the chosen real phase of the
complex representation, not the complete complex quantity.

The real part is defined by the complex decomposition of the electrostatic
potential:

$$
\phi_R = \operatorname{Re}\{\phi\}, \qquad \phi = \phi_R + i\phi_I
$$

where $\phi$ is the complex electrostatic potential, $\phi_R$ is this real
part, and $\phi_I$ is the corresponding imaginary part.

This quantity excludes the imaginary quadrature, the complex modulus, the
phase angle, and any reconstructed physical perturbation obtained after
applying additional mode or time phase factors. The [perturbed
electrostatic-potential real
part](name:perturbed_electrostatic_potential_real_part) is the first-order
perturbation-specific instance of this real-part quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when the real quadrature of the electrostatic
potential is above the chosen scalar-potential reference for the specified
complex phase.

items.name: normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1
items.description:
Normalized perturbed pressure Bessel-1 is the dimensionless total pressure
response of a perturbed gyrocenter distribution in a linear gyrokinetic
eigenmode, formed from parallel and perpendicular pressure moments weighted
by the first-order Bessel function evaluated on the gyroaveraging argument
and normalized to the equilibrium species pressure.
items.documentation:
Normalized perturbed pressure Bessel-1 is the dimensionless total pressure
response of a perturbed gyrocenter distribution in a linear gyrokinetic
eigenmode, formed from parallel and perpendicular pressure moments weighted
by the first-order Bessel function evaluated on the gyroaveraging argument
and normalized to the equilibrium species pressure. It is a species-resolved
complex amplitude representing the finite-Larmor-radius part of the
gyrocenter pressure response.

For species $s$, it is defined by the sum of the first-order Bessel-weighted
parallel and perpendicular pressure moments divided by the equilibrium
species pressure:

$$
\widehat{P}^{(J_1)}_s = \frac{P_{\parallel s}^{(J_1)} + P_{\perp s}^{(J_1)}}{p_s}, \qquad P_{\parallel s}^{(J_1)} = \int d^3v\, m_s v_\parallel^2 J_1(\lambda_s)\widetilde{F}_{g,s}, \qquad P_{\perp s}^{(J_1)} = \int d^3v\, m_s \frac{v_\perp^2}{2} J_1(\lambda_s)\widetilde{F}_{g,s}
$$

where $P_{\parallel s}^{(J_1)}$ and $P_{\perp s}^{(J_1)}$ are
pressure-moment amplitudes with pressure units, $p_s=n_sT_s$ is the
equilibrium species pressure when $T_s$ is expressed as energy per particle,
$m_s$ is the species mass, $v_\parallel$ and $v_\perp$ are velocities
parallel and perpendicular to the equilibrium magnetic field, $d^3v$ is the
velocity-space volume element, and $\widetilde{F}_{g,s}$ is the perturbation
amplitude of the gyrocenter distribution. The first-order Bessel function
$J_1$ is evaluated on the gyroaveraging argument $\lambda_s=k_\perp
v_\perp/\Omega_s$, with $k_\perp$ the magnitude of the wave vector
perpendicular to the equilibrium magnetic field and $\Omega_s=|q_s|B/m_s$
the positive cyclotron-frequency magnitude.

The total moment is the sum of
parallel_normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1 and
[perpendicular_normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1](name:perpendicular_normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1).
It is a gyrocenter-distribution moment with explicit $J_1(\lambda_s)$
weighting; it is distinct from normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure,
which lacks this Bessel-1 weighting, and from particle-distribution pressure
perturbations such as normalized_perturbed_pressure and
normalized_total_particle_perturbed_pressure_of_gyrokinetic_eigenmode.
Because $J_1(0)=0$, this member vanishes at zero gyroaveraging argument.

In a linear eigenmode, $\widetilde{F}_{g,s}$ is the complex coefficient
multiplying the chosen harmonic phase factor. This moment inherits the same
arbitrary global amplitude and phase normalization as the eigenmode;
changing the reference phase multiplies all perturbation amplitudes by the
same complex factor, so its sign and phase are defined only relative to that
reference.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_beryllium_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Number density of beryllium ions averaged over the plasma boundary, summed
over all ionization states and excluding neutral beryllium.
items.documentation:
Number density of beryllium

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{Be}}\rangle = \oint n_{\mathrm{Be}}\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \, /\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $\langle n_{\mathrm{Be}}\rangle$ is the averaged beryllium-ion number
density, $n_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the local beryllium-ion number density, $S$ is
the plasma-boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface element, and $\psi$ is
the poloidal magnetic flux whose gradient magnitude is $|\nabla\psi|$.

This quantity is summed over all beryllium ion charge states and excludes
neutral beryllium. It is a flux-surface average, not a local point value,
volume average, or chord average.

It is the flux-surface-averaged counterpart of the local [beryllium ion
density at the plasma boundary](name:beryllium_density_at_plasma_boundary).
It differs from the [volume-averaged beryllium
density](name:volume_averaged_beryllium_density), which uses a volume rather
than a flux-surface domain.

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

items.name: torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons
items.description:
Torque density due to Coulomb collisions with electrons is the local
toroidal angular-momentum transfer rate per volume to a specified plasma
population caused by Coulomb collisional momentum exchange with electrons.
items.documentation:
Torque density due to Coulomb collisions with electrons is the local
toroidal angular-momentum transfer rate per volume to a specified plasma
population caused by Coulomb collisional momentum exchange with electrons.
It is the torque density about the vertical symmetry axis associated only
with electron collision partners.

The scalar torque density is the moment arm times the toroidal component of
the Coulomb-collisional force density from electrons in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame:

$$
\tau_e^{\mathrm{C}} = R f_{\phi,e}^{\mathrm{C}}
$$

where $R$ is major radius and $f_{\phi,e}^{\mathrm{C}}$ is the toroidal
component, along $\hat{\phi}$, of the force density on the receiving
population due to Coulomb collisions with electrons.

This parent quantity does not specify the receiving population;
species-specific children such as electron torque density due to Coulomb
collisions with electrons identify that population. It excludes torque
density from collisions with ions or neutrals, from external fields or
waves, and from any non-Coulomb momentum-transfer mechanism.

Sign convention: Positive when the Coulomb-collisional force density from
electrons on the receiving population points in the direction of increasing
toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: coolant_temperature_of_plant_component_port
items.description:
Thermodynamic temperature of the working coolant at a generic inlet or
outlet port of a power-conversion component.
items.documentation:
Coolant temperature is the thermodynamic temperature describing the thermal
state of the working fluid at a connection port of a power-conversion
component.

The quantity applies to coolant at a generic plant-component port, which may
be an inlet or an outlet. It denotes the local fluid state at that port; no
summation, spatial averaging, or integration is implied. It excludes the
temperature of the component structure or any other material.

Unlike [coolant temperature at outlet](name:coolant_temperature_at_outlet),
this quantity does not restrict the port to an outlet. It is a thermal-state
quantity, whereas [coolant transit time of plant component
port](name:coolant_transit_time_of_plant_component_port) describes the
elapsed transport time between component ports rather than the coolant
temperature.

items.name: coulomb_logarithm_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Natural logarithm of the effective upper-to-lower impact-parameter ratio
governing cumulative small-angle Coulomb scattering between charged
particles at the pressure pedestal top.
items.documentation:
The Coulomb logarithm at the [pressure pedestal
top](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal) expresses the
effective logarithmic range of impact parameters contributing to cumulative
small-angle Coulomb scattering between charged particles at that location.

Its defining relation is

$$
\ln\Lambda = \ln\left(\frac{b_{\max}}{b_{\min}}\right)
$$

where $\ln\Lambda$ is the local Coulomb logarithm, $\ln$ denotes the natural
logarithm, $\Lambda$ is the effective impact-parameter ratio, $b_{\max}$ is
the upper impact-parameter cutoff associated with plasma screening, and
$b_{\min}$ is the lower cutoff associated with strong deflections or quantum
diffraction, as applicable. Both cutoffs refer to local plasma conditions at
the pressure pedestal top.

This quantity is the local evaluation of the [Coulomb
logarithm](name:coulomb_logarithm), not an average or integral across the
pedestal. No particular colliding species pair is specified.

items.name: toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Signed deuterium-ion fluid velocity along the geometric toroidal direction,
evaluated at the radial location assigned to the internal transport barrier.
items.documentation:
The deuterium-ion toroidal velocity is the projection of the deuterium-ion
fluid velocity onto the geometric toroidal direction at the flux-surface
radius assigned to the internal transport barrier. Neutral deuterium is
excluded. It is the deuterium-specific counterpart of the [toroidal hydrogen
velocity at the internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the defining
projection is

$$
v_{D,\phi} = \mathbf{v}_D \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_D$ is the deuterium-ion fluid velocity, $\hat{\phi}$ is
the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, and
$v_{D,\phi}$ is evaluated at the internal-transport-barrier location.

Sign convention: Positive when the deuterium-ion flow has a component in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: tungsten_density_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Tungsten ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the
local concentration of ionized tungsten, summed over all tungsten charge
states.
items.documentation:
Tungsten ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the
local concentration of ionized tungsten at the inner shoulder of the H-mode
transport barrier.

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{W}} = \sum_{q=1}^{Z_{\mathrm{W}}} n_{\mathrm{W}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{W}}$ is the total tungsten-ion number density, $q$ is the
positive tungsten charge state, $Z_{\mathrm{W}}$ is the atomic number of
tungsten, and $n_{\mathrm{W}^{q+}}$ is the number density of tungsten ions
in charge state $q$. Neutral tungsten is excluded.

This quantity applies to the local tungsten-ion population at the pedestal
top, whose position is defined by the [normalized poloidal-flux coordinate
at the pedestal top](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal).
It is summed over all positive tungsten charge states and is neither
flux-surface averaged nor line-of-sight averaged.

It is the tungsten-specific component of [density at the pedestal
top](name:density_at_pedestal_top). Unlike [tungsten density at the internal
transport barrier](name:tungsten_density_at_internal_transport_barrier),
which is evaluated on an internal-transport-barrier flux surface, this
quantity is evaluated at the pedestal-top location.

items.name: ion_momentum_damping_rate
items.description:
Effective inverse relaxation time for collisional and neoclassical
dissipation of bulk ion fluid momentum, expressed as a vector whose
components each quantify the damping rate along a distinct geometric
projection of the ion velocity.
items.documentation:
The ion momentum damping rate is the effective inverse relaxation timescale
at which ordered bulk ion fluid momentum is dissipated through Coulomb
collisions and neoclassical viscous stresses. As a vector, it encodes the
geometric anisotropy of momentum loss in a magnetized plasma, where the
field-aligned and toroidal projections relax through distinct mechanisms
compared with the poloidal or radial projections.

In the ion fluid momentum balance the damping contribution enters as:

$$\frac{\partial \mathbf{p}_i}{\partial t}\bigg|_{\rm damp} = -\boldsymbol{\nu}_D^{\,i} \cdot \mathbf{p}_i$$

where $\mathbf{p}_i = m_i n_i \mathbf{v}_i$ is the ion momentum density,
with $m_i$ the ion mass, $n_i$ the number density, and $\mathbf{v}_i$ the
bulk ion fluid velocity. The rate $\boldsymbol{\nu}_D^{\,i}$ is applied
component-wise and aggregates contributions from all ion charge states.

Component-resolved scalar rates are
[radial_ion_momentum_damping_rate](name:radial_ion_momentum_damping_rate),
[toroidal_ion_momentum_damping_rate](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_damping_rate),
[poloidal_ion_momentum_damping_rate](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_damping_rate),
and
[parallel_ion_momentum_damping_rate](name:parallel_ion_momentum_damping_rate).
These are computed from neoclassical transport theory or
turbulent-momentum-transport models. This quantity serves as the
ion-species-level structural parent described by
[momentum_damping_rate](name:momentum_damping_rate), which covers the
general multi-species case.

items.name: ion_state_mean_ionisation_potential
items.description:
Concentration-weighted mean cumulative energy required to reach the charge
states in an ion-state bundle by successive ionization from the neutral
ground state.
items.documentation:
Ion-state mean ionization potential is the concentration-weighted mean of
the cumulative successive ionization energies required to reach, from the
neutral ground state, the charge states represented in an ion-state bundle.
It expresses the mean ionization energy per particle associated with the
bundle's charge-state composition.

For a populated bundle, the mean is defined by:

$$
\bar{E}_{\mathrm{ion},s} = \frac{\displaystyle\sum_{q\in\mathcal{B}_s} n_q \displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{q} I_k}{\displaystyle\sum_{q\in\mathcal{B}_s} n_q}
$$

where $\bar{E}_{\mathrm{ion},s}$ is the mean cumulative ionization potential
of bundle $s$, $\mathcal{B}_s$ is its set of represented charge states, $q$
is the ionic charge number, $n_q$ is the number density of that charge
state, $k$ indexes successive ionization steps, and $I_k$ is the
ground-state ionization energy for the transition from charge number $k-1$
to $k$. The cumulative energy of the neutral ground state is zero.

The averaging includes only the charge states represented in the specified
bundle of one ion species and requires a nonzero total bundle number
density. For a bundle containing a single charge state, the mean reduces to
that state's cumulative ionization energy, not the threshold energy for
removing its next electron.

This quantity excludes thermal internal energy, excitation energy, radiation
losses, and kinetic energy exchanged during ionization or recombination. The
[change in ion-state mean ionization potential] is the value after a
specified state change minus the value before it for the same bundle.

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_arc_of_circle_center
items.description:
Major-radius coordinate of an iron-core segment’s annular cross-section
center in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the major-radius coordinate $R$ of the center of the
annular cross-section representing one iron-core segment. It identifies the
radial placement of that annular center in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and
$Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity is defined separately for each segment’s annulus center; it is
neither averaged nor summed over segments. It denotes the center coordinate
rather than the major-radius coordinate of an arc start point, arc endpoint,
or arbitrary outline point.

The [radial outline of the iron-core
segment](name:radial_outline_of_iron_core_segment) gives major-radius
coordinates for points on the cross-sectional boundary, whereas this
quantity gives the major-radius coordinate used to locate the annular
center.

items.name: toroidal_neon_velocity_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Toroidal component of the density-weighted neon-ion fluid velocity at the
core-side top of the H-mode edge transport barrier.
items.documentation:
Toroidal neon-ion velocity at the H-mode pedestal top is the
density-weighted mean of the toroidal fluid velocities of all represented
neon ion charge states at the core-side shoulder of the edge transport
barrier. It is a signed projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame.

$$
V_{\mathrm{Ne},\phi} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ne},q} v_{\mathrm{Ne},q,\phi}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ne},q}}
$$

Here, $q$ labels neon ion charge state, $n_{\mathrm{Ne},q}$ is its number
density, and $v_{\mathrm{Ne},q,\phi}$ is its toroidal fluid-velocity
component. The quantity is distinguished from [toroidal neon velocity at the
internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier) by its
pedestal-top location and is a species-specific counterpart of [toroidal
hydrogen velocity at the pedestal
top](name:toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_pedestal_top).

Sign convention: Positive when the neon-ion flow has a component in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: beryllium_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
items.description:
Instantaneous equivalent-electron source rate of beryllium atoms introduced
by gas injection, with four equivalent electrons assigned to each atom.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the instantaneous rate of beryllium supplied by gas
injection, represented using an equivalent-electron counting convention. It
describes injected beryllium input rather than the creation rate of free
plasma electrons or a time-integrated beryllium inventory.

The equivalent-electron rate is defined from the beryllium atom injection
rate by

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq,Be}}(t) = Z_{\mathrm{Be}}\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Be}}(t)
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq,Be}}$ is the equivalent-electron count assigned to
injected beryllium, $N_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the number of injected beryllium
atoms, $Z_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the atomic number of beryllium, $t$ is time, and
the dot denotes differentiation with respect to time. For beryllium,
$Z_{\mathrm{Be}}=4$.

The scope is beryllium delivered by gas injection alone, aggregated over all
injected beryllium atoms. It excludes source contributions from other
species and other injection mechanisms, and it is not a
charge-state-resolved plasma source; the equivalent-electron convention
assigns four counts per injected beryllium atom.

This is the beryllium-specific member of the gas-injection source-rate
family, using the same equivalent-electron basis as the [hydrogen
gas-injection source rate](name:hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection),
[helium-4 gas-injection source
rate](name:helium_4_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection), and [lithium
gas-injection source rate](name:lithium_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection).
Unlike the broader [electron source rate due to
injection](name:electron_source_rate_due_to_injection), it isolates the
nuclear-charge-weighted beryllium contribution. Integrating this
instantaneous rate over a time interval gives the corresponding accumulated
equivalent-electron inventory.

items.name: neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity
items.description:
Effective transport velocity multiplying the thermal energy-density factor
to give the convective energy flux of one neutral species in a specified
internal state.
items.documentation:
The neutral internal-state energy convection velocity is the effective
vector coefficient describing convective thermal-energy transport by one
neutral species in a specified internal state. It is the population-resolved
specialization of [energy convection
velocity](name:energy_convection_velocity), without restriction to a
particular direction.

The convective contribution is defined by:

$$
\mathbf{Q}_{0,a,\mathrm{conv}} = W_{0,a}\mathbf{v}_{0,a,W} = n_{0,a}T_{0,a}\mathbf{v}_{0,a,W}
$$

where $\mathbf{Q}_{0,a,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective thermal-energy
flux, $\mathbf{v}_{0,a,W}$ is this energy convection velocity, and
$W_{0,a}=n_{0,a}T_{0,a}$ is the thermal energy-density factor used in the
transport closure. Here $n_{0,a}$ is the population number density and
$T_{0,a}$ is its temperature expressed as an energy; the subscript $0$
identifies neutrals and $a$ identifies the specified internal state of the
selected species.

This quantity is resolved by neutral species and internal state, with no sum
or average over either. Its flux contribution excludes gradient-driven
diffusion and any separately specified energy transport proportional to the
particle flux; it therefore does not represent the total energy flux. As an
effective energy-channel coefficient, it need not equal the [bulk neutral
internal-state velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity).

The [parallel
component](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity)
and [poloidal
component](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity)
are directional projections of this vector for the same population. The
poloidal direction is defined in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$,
where $\rho$ labels magnetic flux surfaces, $\theta$ is the poloidal angle,
and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle.

Sign convention: Positive when the parallel component transports thermal
energy along the local magnetic field, or the poloidal component transports
thermal energy toward increasing $\theta$.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_lithium_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Number density of lithium ions averaged over the plasma-boundary flux
surface, summed over all lithium ion charge states and excluding neutral
lithium.
items.documentation:
Number density of lithium

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{Li}}\rangle = \oint n_{\mathrm{Li}}\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \, / \, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $\langle n_{\mathrm{Li}}\rangle$ is the averaged lithium-ion number
density, $n_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the local lithium-ion number density, $S$ is
the plasma-boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface element, $\psi$ is
poloidal magnetic flux, and $\nabla$ denotes the spatial gradient operator,
so $|\nabla\psi|$ is the magnitude of that gradient.

This quantity applies to lithium ions on the plasma boundary and is summed
over all positive lithium ion charge states. It excludes neutral lithium and
is not a local point value, a volume average, or a line-of-sight average.

It is the flux-surface-averaged counterpart of the local [lithium-ion number
density at the plasma boundary](name:lithium_density_at_plasma_boundary),
replacing the pointwise value with inverse-poloidal-flux-gradient weighting
over the surface. It differs from the [volume-averaged lithium
density](name:volume_averaged_lithium_density), which averages over plasma
volume, and the [line-averaged lithium
density](name:line_averaged_lithium_density), which averages along a
specified chord.

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

items.name: line_averaged_carbon_density
items.description:
Line-averaged total number density of elemental carbon along a specified
plasma chord, summed over neutral carbon and all ionic charge states through
C6+.
items.documentation:
Line-averaged carbon density is the chord average of the total number
density of elemental carbon, encompassing neutral carbon atoms and all ionic
charge states from singly ionized C+ through fully stripped C6+.

It is defined from the local [carbon density](name:carbon_density) along the
chord:

$$
\bar n_C = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_C(\ell)\,d\ell = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L \sum_{z=0}^{6} n_{C^{z+}}(\ell)\,d\ell
$$

where $\bar n_C$ is the line-averaged carbon density, $n_C(\ell)$ is the
local carbon density in m$^{-3}$, $n_{C^{z+}}(\ell)$ is the local density of
carbon charge state $z+$ in m$^{-3}$, $\ell$ is distance along the chord in
m, and $L$ is the chord length in m. This chord average is distinct from
[volume-averaged carbon density](name:volume_averaged_carbon_density), which
averages over the confined plasma volume.

items.name: volume_of_first_wall
items.description:
Volume enclosed by the first-wall surface, representing the interior region
inside the innermost plasma-facing boundary rather than the wall material
itself.
items.documentation:
The first-wall volume is the total interior volume enclosed by the innermost
plasma-facing surface of the vacuum vessel. It includes the space available
to the confined plasma, edge and scrape-off-layer regions, and neutral gas,
but excludes the material volume of the wall.

For an axisymmetric first-wall contour in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the volume is defined by

$$
V_{\rm FW}=2\pi\iint_A R\,dR\,dZ
$$

where $A$ is the poloidal cross-sectional area enclosed by the first-wall
contour, $R$ is major radius in meters, and $Z$ is vertical height in
meters. For non-axisymmetric geometry, the complete three-dimensional
enclosed region, including bounded ports and recesses, defines the volume.

This enclosed volume is distinct from [volume enclosed by the plasma
boundary](name:volume_of_flux_surface), which is limited by the last closed
flux surface, and from [area of the first wall](name:area_of_first_wall),
which measures the wall's material surface rather than an enclosed region.

items.name: krypton_density_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Particle number density of the krypton ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local krypton-ion count per physical volume at that
location.
items.documentation:
Particle number density of the krypton ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local krypton-ion count per physical volume at that
location. It represents krypton ions specifically, summed over all ionic
charge states and excluding neutral krypton.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Kr,axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{Kr}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Kr,axis}}$ is the krypton-ion number density at the
magnetic axis, $N_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the number of krypton ions summed over
ionic charge states, $V$ is physical volume, and the subscript axis denotes
evaluation at the magnetic axis.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the complete krypton-ion population at that
location, with number density summed over all krypton ionic charge states;
it is neither a flux-surface or volume integral nor a density of neutral
krypton, electrons, or other ion species.

This is the krypton-specific realization of the population-independent
[density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). The [neon
density at the magnetic axis](name:neon_density_at_magnetic_axis) has the
same local locus and charge-state-summed convention but counts neon ions
rather than krypton ions.

items.name: plasma_momentum
items.description:
Plasma momentum is the volume-integrated linear momentum carried by the
included plasma species, for the component, projection, or aggregate
specified by a qualified child name. It is an extensive momentum integral,
not kinetic energy, angular momentum, or momentum flux.
items.documentation:
Plasma momentum is the linear momentum carried by plasma matter after
integration over the stated plasma volume. For a scalar standard name it
denotes the specified component or projection of that integrated momentum; a
qualified aggregate such as [total plasma
momentum](name:total_plasma_momentum) denotes the corresponding net plasma
momentum rather than an axis-specific value.

For component or projection label $\alpha$, the plasma momentum is defined
by the volume integral of species momentum density:

$$
P_\alpha = \int_V \sum_s m_s n_s(\mathbf{x}) v_{s,\alpha}(\mathbf{x}) \, dV
$$

where $P_\alpha$ is the plasma momentum component or projection labeled by
$\alpha$, $V$ is the plasma volume, $s$ indexes the included plasma species,
$m_s$ is the particle mass of species $s$, $n_s$ is the number density of
species $s$, $v_{s,\alpha}$ is the corresponding component or projection of
the species flow velocity, and $dV$ is a volume element.

This quantity is extensive over the included plasma volume and additive over
the included species. It excludes angular momentum, momentum flux or stress,
kinetic energy, and electromagnetic field momentum unless a more specific
qualified name explicitly changes that scope.

Sign convention: Positive when the scalar component or projection of the
volume-integrated species momentum points in the positive direction named by
the qualified standard name.

items.name: absorbed_radiated_power_at_wall
items.description:
Net radiative power deposited on plasma-facing wall surfaces, equal to
incident plasma radiation minus the portion reflected back toward the
plasma.
items.documentation:
Net absorbed radiative power is the total photon power retained by
plasma-facing wall surfaces after reflection losses. It represents the
wall's radiative power load and excludes nonradiative particle, conductive,
and other thermal-power contributions.

The net retained power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{abs,wall}} = P_{\mathrm{inc,wall}} - P_{\mathrm{ref,wall}}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{abs,wall}}$ is the absorbed radiative power at the wall,
$P_{\mathrm{inc,wall}}$ is the total plasma-radiation power incident on the
wall, and $P_{\mathrm{ref,wall}}$ is the portion of that incident radiation
reflected away from the wall. The quantity is integrated over the wall
rather than expressed as a local power per unit area.

This wall-wide quantity includes the aggregate radiative load over all
applicable plasma-facing wall surfaces. It is broader than [absorbed
radiated power of divertor](name:absorbed_radiated_power_of_divertor) and
[absorbed radiated power of breeder blanket
module](name:absorbed_radiated_power_of_breeder_blanket_module), which apply
the same incident-minus-reflected principle to specified wall components,
and it is distinct from [total incident neutral energy flux at
wall](name:total_incident_neutral_energy_flux_at_wall), which describes
neutral-particle energy transport rather than absorbed photon power.

items.name: parallel_fast_neutral_pressure
items.description:
Pressure of suprathermal neutrals of one species is the
magnetic-field-parallel normal component of their kinetic pressure tensor.
It is summed over internal quantum and excitation states and, where multiple
charge-state contributions are represented, over charge states.
items.documentation:
Pressure of suprathermal neutrals of one species is the field-aligned normal
component of their kinetic pressure tensor. The local magnetic-field
direction defines the projection axis; this is a directional component, not
an isotropic scalar pressure.

The parallel component is the projection of the kinetic pressure tensor onto
that direction:

$$
p_{0,\mathrm{fast},\parallel} = \hat{\mathbf b} \cdot \mathbf P_{0,\mathrm{fast}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf b}
$$

where $p_{0,\mathrm{fast},\parallel}$ is this parallel fast-neutral
pressure, $\mathbf P_{0,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the kinetic pressure tensor of
the suprathermal neutral population, and $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the unit
vector along the local magnetic field $\mathbf B$.

The quantity applies to suprathermal neutrals of one species. Contributions
are summed over all internal quantum and excitation states and, when
multiple charge-state contributions are represented, over all charge states;
this is an additive sum, not an average. It excludes thermal-neutral
pressure and pressure from other species. Unlike the [parallel fast-neutral
internal-state
pressure](name:parallel_fast_neutral_internal_state_pressure), it is not
resolved by a single internal state.

This is a directional component, distinct from the isotropic trace quantity
[fast-neutral pressure](name:fast_neutral_pressure). Together with
[perpendicular fast-neutral
pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_neutral_pressure), it specifies the
gyrotropic pressure decomposition; the parallel and perpendicular components
need not be equal.

items.name: time_derivative_of_total_thermal_plasma_internal_energy
items.description:
Temporal rate of change of the plasma’s total thermal internal energy,
representing net thermal power deposited into or removed from the plasma.
items.documentation:
The time derivative of total thermal plasma internal energy is the net
temporal rate at which the aggregate thermal energy of the plasma changes.
Positive accumulation denotes increasing thermal energy, while negative
accumulation denotes net thermal-energy loss.

$$
P_{\mathrm{net,th}}(t) = \frac{dU_{\mathrm{th,pl}}(t)}{dt}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{net,th}}$ is the total thermal-energy change rate,
$U_{\mathrm{th,pl}}$ is the total thermal internal energy of the plasma, and
$t$ is time.

The underlying energy is integrated over the plasma volume and aggregated
over the included thermal plasma populations. It excludes
nonthermal-particle energy, bulk-flow kinetic energy, and
electromagnetic-field energy; it is not restricted to a single species or
energy-transfer channel.

This quantity is the time derivative of [total thermal plasma internal
energy](name:total_thermal_plasma_internal_energy). It is a global
thermal-energy balance quantity, distinct from [volume-integrated electron
power density](name:volume_integrated_electron_power_density), which is
restricted to the electron population, and from [power at inside flux
surface](name:power_at_inside_flux_surface), which is associated with a
specified enclosed region.

Sign convention: Positive when the total thermal plasma internal energy
increases with time.

items.name: poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part
items.description:
Real part of the complex poloidal component of the first-order plasma
magnetic-field perturbation eigenfunction for a specified toroidal Fourier
mode in linear MHD stability analysis.
items.documentation:
The poloidal perturbed plasma magnetic field real part gives the in-phase
component of the complex eigenfunction projection $\delta B_\theta =
\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{pl} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta$, where
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta$ is the poloidal unit vector in flux coordinates
$(\psi, \theta, \phi)$, with $\psi$ the poloidal magnetic flux, $\theta$ the
poloidal angle, and $\phi$ the toroidal angle.

The defining relation is:

$$
\mathrm{Re}(\delta B_\theta) = \mathrm{Re}\!\left[\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{pl} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta\right]
$$

where $\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{pl}$ is the first-order plasma
magnetic-field perturbation eigenfunction for a single toroidal mode number
$n$ and $\delta B_\theta$ has unit T.

Together with
[poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part),
this quantity fully specifies the complex poloidal eigenfunction component.
The counterpart quantities
[radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part)
and
[toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part)
complete the vector decomposition of $\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{pl}$.
Absolute eigenfunction amplitudes depend on normalization convention;
physically meaningful results are obtained from spatial ratios between
components and from plasma-to-vacuum matching against
[poloidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part](name:poloidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part).

Sign convention: Positive when the real part of
$\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{pl} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta$ is directed in
the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

items.name: iron_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Number density of iron impurity ions at the plasma boundary, the last closed
flux surface separating the magnetically confined plasma from the
open-field-line scrape-off layer, summed over all ion charge states from Fe+
through fully stripped Fe26+.
items.documentation:
Iron density at the plasma boundary is the number of iron impurity ions per
unit volume — summed over all ion charge states from singly ionized Fe$^+$
through fully stripped Fe$^{26+}$ (atomic number $Z = 26$) — evaluated at
the separatrix, the last closed flux surface separating the magnetically
confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer. It represents the
charge-state-summed iron impurity concentration on that boundary.

The charge-state aggregation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Fe}} = \sum_{z=1}^{26} n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the iron ion number density at the plasma
boundary, $z$ is the positive ion charge state, and $n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}$
is the partial number density of iron ions in charge state $z+$ at the same
boundary; these number-density variables have the unit specified for this
standard name.

The sum is over ion charge states only, so neutral iron Fe$^0$ is excluded.
As a scalar number density, the quantity is non-negative, with zero denoting
absence of iron ions at the plasma boundary. It is distinct from
flux_surface_averaged_iron_density_at_plasma_boundary, which denotes a
flux-surface-averaged boundary value rather than the local boundary density.

items.name: deuterium_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Number density of deuterium ions at the radial location of the internal
transport barrier, where suppressed turbulent cross-field transport enables
steep fuel-species density gradients to develop.
items.documentation:
Deuterium density at the internal transport barrier is the local number
density of deuterium ions on the flux surface assigned as the barrier
reference location. Deuterium ($^2$H, mass number $A = 2$) is the heavier
hydrogen isotope used as primary fuel in magnetic-confinement fusion and is
fully ionized to D$^+$ in the hot plasma core, requiring no summation over
charge states.

An internal transport barrier is a radially localized region of reduced
cross-field turbulent transport within the confined plasma, enabling steep
radial gradients in particle density and temperature to be sustained. The
deuterium density at the barrier is the point value of the local number
density $n_D(\rho)$ evaluated at the normalized minor radius
$\rho_\mathrm{ITB}$ of the barrier:

$$
n_D^\mathrm{ITB} = n_D(\rho_\mathrm{ITB})
$$

where $\rho_\mathrm{ITB}$ is identified by the location of the maximum
logarithmic gradient in the density or temperature profile.

This quantity is inferred from main-ion charge-exchange recombination
spectroscopy, or derived from transport analysis constrained by Thomson
scattering and interferometry, with the steep gradients at the ITB making
precise radial localization critical. It is the deuterium-isotope
counterpart to
[hydrogen_density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:hydrogen_density_at_internal_transport_barrier);
together they represent the two lightest hydrogenic fuel species. The full
family of species-specific barrier densities is described by
[density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier),
and
[electron_density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:electron_density_at_internal_transport_barrier)
provides the quasi-neutral electron counterpart.

items.name: trapped_fast_current_density
items.description:
Trapped fast-particle current density is the vector electric current density
carried by fast particles on magnetically trapped orbits, excluding
compensating electron and thermal-ion return currents.
items.documentation:
Trapped fast-particle current density is the contribution to electric
current density from fast particles whose guiding-center orbits are
magnetically trapped. It excludes compensating currents carried by electrons
and thermal ions and is not the total plasma current density.

At position $\mathbf{x}$, its kinetic definition is

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{trap}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_s q_s \int_{\mathrm{trapped, fast}} \mathbf{v}\, f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,\mathrm{d}^3v
$$

where $q_s$ is the charge of species $s$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity,
and $f_s$ is its phase-space distribution. The integration is restricted to
the trapped fast-particle population. This quantity is an orbit-selected
contribution to [fast current density](name:fast_current_density); [toroidal
trapped fast current density](name:toroidal_trapped_fast_current_density) is
its toroidal component, while [co-passing fast current
density](name:co_passing_fast_current_density) represents a distinct
passing-orbit contribution.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved component of the conventional
electric current-density vector points along the corresponding positive
direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ basis.

items.name: poloidal_neutral_internal_state_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Effective poloidal particle diffusivity for neutral atoms or molecules in a
specified internal state, relating poloidal diffusive flux to that state's
physical number-density gradient along the poloidal direction in flux
coordinates (ρ, θ, φ).
items.documentation:
The poloidal component of the neutral internal-state diffusion coefficient
governs Fickian particle transport of neutral atoms or molecules in a
specified internal state along the poloidal direction of flux coordinates
$(\rho, \theta, \phi)$. It is the proportionality coefficient between the
signed poloidal diffusive particle flux and the physical poloidal gradient
of that state's number density.

For a neutral internal state $s$, the poloidal Fickian relation is

$$
\Gamma_{\theta,s}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{\theta,s}\,\frac{1}{h_\theta}\frac{\partial n_s}{\partial \theta}
$$

where $D_{\theta,s}$ is the poloidal neutral internal-state diffusion
coefficient, $\Gamma_{\theta,s}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the poloidal diffusive
particle-flux component, $n_s$ is the number density of neutral atoms or
molecules in internal state $s$, and $h_\theta =
|\partial\mathbf{x}/\partial\theta|_{\rho,\phi}$ is the poloidal metric
scale factor for flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$. The factor
$h_\theta^{-1}\partial/\partial\theta$ is the derivative along physical
poloidal arc length, not a bare angular derivative.

This coefficient applies only to particle-number diffusion of the specified
neutral internal state. It excludes momentum diffusion, energy diffusion,
radial diffusion, and off-diagonal transport couplings unless such effects
are explicitly represented as part of the effective scalar coefficient.

Sign convention: Positive when the poloidal diffusive particle flux is
opposite to the physical poloidal gradient of the state number density, with
a positive flux component pointing toward increasing poloidal coordinate
$\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$.

items.name: accumulated_xenon_prefill_count
items.description:
Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of neutral xenon introduced during
plasma prefill, ending at plasma breakdown, with 54 count units per atom.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the equivalent-electron inventory of neutral xenon gas
introduced between the start of prefill and plasma breakdown. It represents
the accumulated prefill contribution, not an instantaneous injection rate.

The defining accumulation is

$$
N_{\mathrm{Xe,eq}}^{\mathrm{prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{Xe}} \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Xe}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Xe}}(t)$ is the neutral xenon atom injection rate,
$t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the prefill start and breakdown times, and
$Z_{\mathrm{Xe}}=54$ is xenon's atomic number. The resulting count assigns
54 equivalent-electron units to each xenon atom.

This quantity is the prefill component of xenon_prefill_count and excludes
xenon introduced after breakdown, which is represented by
accumulated_xenon_count.

items.name: total_external_heating_power
items.description:
Total non-inductive power coupled from external neutral-beam and
radio-frequency heating systems to the plasma, summed over auxiliary sources
and excluding Ohmic heating.
items.documentation:
Total external heating power is the aggregate non-inductive power coupled to
the plasma by auxiliary heating systems. It includes neutral-beam injection
and electron-cyclotron, ion-cyclotron, and lower-hybrid systems, while
excluding power associated with Ohmic induction.

The defining aggregate relation is

$$
P_{\mathrm{ext}} = \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aux}}} P_s
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{ext}}$ is the total external heating power,
$\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aux}}$ is the set of included auxiliary heating
systems, and $P_s$ is the power coupled to the plasma by auxiliary source
$s$.

The quantity applies to the whole plasma and is summed over all included
auxiliary sources rather than resolved by source, species, or spatial
region. It represents external power input that may contribute to both
plasma heating and non-inductive current drive; it is distinct from Ohmic
heating and from generator power that is not coupled to the plasma.
Source-specific contributions include [total power due to electron-cyclotron
heating](name:total_power_due_to_electron_cyclotron_heating), [total power
due to ion-cyclotron
heating](name:total_power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating), and power absorbed
from a neutral-beam injector, whose aggregate forms contribute to the sum.

items.name: krypton_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Number density of krypton ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated as the
local, intensive particle count per physical volume on the last closed
magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
Number density of krypton ions at the plasma boundary is the local,
intensive particle count per physical volume for the krypton-ion population
evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is
the limiting closed magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from
the open-field-line scrape-off-layer region.

The local krypton ion number density is the sum of the zeroth velocity
moments over all krypton ionization states at a boundary point:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Kr}}(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \sum_{q \in \mathcal{Q}_{\mathrm{Kr}}} \int f_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the krypton ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is
a point on the last closed magnetic flux surface, $t$ is time, $q$ is the
krypton ionization-state index, $\mathcal{Q}_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the set of
all positively charged krypton ionization states, $f_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}$ is
the phase-space distribution function for state $q$, $\mathbf{v}$ is
particle velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies specifically to krypton ions and is summed over all
included ionization states. It excludes neutral krypton and all other ion
species, and it is a local boundary value with no averaging over the
boundary surface or over a volume.

It is the krypton-specific instance of [density at the plasma
boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). The related [krypton
density](name:krypton_density) represents the same charge-state-summed ion
population at a general plasma location, whereas flux-surface-averaged
krypton density at the plasma boundary averages the krypton density over the
complete last closed magnetic flux surface rather than evaluating it
locally.

items.name: toroidal_wave_electric_field
items.description:
Complex phasor component of an electromagnetic-wave electric field projected
onto the toroidal direction, preserving local amplitude, phase, and toroidal
polarization.
items.documentation:
The toroidal wave electric field is the complex phasor obtained by
projecting the electromagnetic-wave electric-field phasor onto the toroidal
direction. It retains the local amplitude and phase of the toroidal
component of the [wave electric field](name:wave_electric_field).

For a single angular frequency, the toroidal component is defined by

$$
\widetilde{E}_{\phi}(\mathbf{r},\omega)=\widetilde{\mathbf{E}}_{\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{r},\omega)\cdot\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\widetilde{E}_{\phi}$ is the toroidal component phasor,
$\widetilde{\mathbf{E}}_{\mathrm{wave}}$ is the complex wave-electric-field
phasor, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, $\omega$ is angular frequency, and
$\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

This quantity is the wave contribution only and is distinct from the total
[toroidal electric field](name:toroidal_electric_field). Its axis projection
is analogous to the [vertical wave electric
field](name:vertical_wave_electric_field), but it represents the component
along increasing toroidal angle rather than the vertical direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the projected electric-field vector points in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: volume_averaged_hydrogen_density
items.description:
Volume-averaged number density of hydrogen (protium) ions in the plasma,
giving the mean H+ concentration across the confined plasma volume.
items.documentation:
The volume-averaged hydrogen density quantifies the mean concentration of
ionized protium throughout the confined plasma volume. It is the spatial
average of the local [hydrogen density](name:hydrogen_density), rather than
its value at a particular position.

$$
\overline{n}_H = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_H(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $\overline{n}_H$ is the volume-averaged hydrogen density,
$n_H(\mathbf{r})$ is the local ionized-protium density at position
$\mathbf{r}$, $V_p$ is the confined plasma volume, and $dV$ is a volume
element. The average includes ionized protium throughout $V_p$ and excludes
neutral atomic hydrogen and other isotopes. Unlike [line-averaged hydrogen
density](name:line_averaged_hydrogen_density), it averages over the full
plasma volume. Its isotope fraction relative to all hydrogenic fuel is
represented by [the volume-averaged hydrogen-density
fraction](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_hydrogen_density_to_volume_averaged_total_hydrogenic_density).

items.name: thermal_ion_density
items.description:
Number density of thermal ions in a selected species or species group,
summed over all positive charge states and excluding fast ions and neutral
particles.
items.documentation:
Number density of ion

For a selected ion species, the charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{i,\mathrm{th}} = \sum_{q\geq 1} n_{i,q,\mathrm{th}}
$$

where $i$ labels the selected ion species, $n_{i,\mathrm{th}}$ is its
thermal ion number density, $q$ is the positive integer charge-state number,
and $n_{i,q,\mathrm{th}}$ is the [thermal ion charge-state number
density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_number_density) for species $i$ in
charge state $q$.

The sum includes all positive charge states and excludes neutral particles.
Both trapped and passing thermal ions are included, while fast, nonthermal
ions are excluded. No spatial averaging or uniformity on a magnetic flux
surface is implied.

For a specified species group, the individual species densities are added;
[total thermal ion density](name:total_thermal_ion_density) is the special
case summed over all ion species. This quantity is the thermal-population
contribution to [ion density](name:ion_density). The thermal contribution
and [fast ion density](name:fast_ion_density) together recover ion density
when these two populations exhaust the selected ion population.

items.name: ion_average_temperature_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Kinetic temperature of the charged-ion population at an internal transport
barrier, defined as the arithmetic mean of charged-ion species temperatures,
excluding electrons and neutral species.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the arithmetic mean of the kinetic temperatures of all
charged ion species on the flux surface assigned to an internal transport
barrier. It retains the locus and population scope of average temperature at
an internal transport barrier.

$$
T_{i,\mathrm{avg}} = \frac{1}{N_i}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{C}} T_{i,s}
$$

where $\mathcal{C}$ is the set of included charged ion species, $N_i$ is the
number of species in that set, and $T_{i,s}$ is the kinetic temperature of
species $s$. For each species, $T_{i,s}$ is the density-weighted mean over
its charge-state temperatures, using $T_{i,s}=\sum_Z n_{s,Z}T_{s,Z}/\sum_Z
n_{s,Z}$, where $n_{s,Z}$ is the number density of charge state $Z$ and
$T_{s,Z}$ is its [ion charge-state
temperature](name:ion_charge_state_temperature). Charge-state weighting is
therefore applied within each species, but distinct ion species are averaged
equally; electrons and neutral species are excluded.

items.name: toroidal_magnetic_flux
items.description:
Toroidal magnetic flux is the signed integral of the toroidal magnetic field
through the poloidal cross-section enclosed by a specified magnetic flux
surface.
items.documentation:
Toroidal magnetic flux is the net flux of the toroidal magnetic-field
component through the poloidal cross-section enclosed by a specified
magnetic flux surface. It specializes [magnetic flux](name:magnetic_flux) by
selecting a surface whose normal points in the toroidal direction.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, it is defined
by

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}} = \int_{\Omega} \mathbf{B}\cdot\hat{\phi}\,dA_{RZ} = \int_{\Omega} B_\phi\,dA_{RZ}
$$

where $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is toroidal magnetic flux, $\Omega$ is the
poloidal cross-sectional region enclosed by the selected magnetic flux
surface, $\mathbf{B}$ is the total magnetic field, $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit
vector toward increasing toroidal angle, $B_\phi$ is the toroidal
magnetic-field component, and $dA_{RZ}$ is the positive poloidal
cross-sectional area element.

The integral includes both externally imposed toroidal field and the field
associated with plasma poloidal current, rather than only a selected source
contribution. It is cumulative inside the selected flux surface, vanishes as
that surface contracts to the magnetic axis, and becomes [toroidal magnetic
flux at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary)
when the selected surface is the plasma boundary. It is neither the
geometric toroidal angle nor a flux-surface average.

Unlike [poloidal magnetic flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux), which threads
a horizontal disk centered on the symmetry axis, toroidal magnetic flux
threads a poloidal cross-section. The [difference of poloidal and toroidal
magnetic flux] is $\psi^* = \psi - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}$, where $\psi$ is
poloidal magnetic flux and $\psi^*$ is the combined flux coordinate. The
[post-sawtooth-crash
difference](name:difference_of_poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_post_sawtooth_crash_and_toroidal_magnetic_flux)
uses the post-crash poloidal flux without changing this definition of
toroidal flux.

Sign convention: Positive when the net toroidal magnetic field threading the
enclosed poloidal cross-section points toward increasing toroidal angle
$\phi$, counterclockwise viewed from above.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_detector_pixel
items.description:
Vertical coordinate at a detector pixel specifies its signed height from the
zero-height plane in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Vertical coordinate at a detector pixel is its signed height relative to the
zero-height plane in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. Here
$R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height
along the toroidal symmetry axis.

The coordinate is defined by

$$
Z = \mathbf{x}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is the detector-pixel position vector measured from the
coordinate origin and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector parallel to the
symmetry axis toward increasing $Z$.

The quantity applies separately to each detector-pixel position, without
averaging over pixels. It is a point coordinate, not the vertical extent of
a pixel or a coordinate along a detector-local tangent direction.

The [toroidal coordinate at the detector
pixel](name:toroidal_coordinate_at_detector_pixel) supplies the angular
coordinate of the same position about the symmetry axis, whereas this
quantity supplies its vertical coordinate.

Sign convention: Positive when the detector pixel lies on the $+Z$ side of
the zero-height plane.

items.name: radial_length_of_divertor_target
items.description:
Non-negative span of a divertor target’s plasma-facing surface along the
major-radius direction, measured between its minimum and maximum R
coordinates.
items.documentation:
The radial span of a divertor target is the extent of its plasma-facing
surface along the major-radius direction. It is a geometric extent, not the
distance along the target surface or a power-deposition width. The direction
is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame with basis
$(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$.

For the plasma-facing surface $S$, the span is defined by

$$
L_R = \max_{\mathbf{x}\in S} R(\mathbf{x}) - \min_{\mathbf{x}\in S} R(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is a point on $S$ and $R(\mathbf{x})$ is its major-radius
coordinate. The quantity includes the full specified target surface and is
non-negative. It complements the [vertical length of the divertor
target](name:vertical_length_of_divertor_target), which uses the extrema of
$Z$, while the [x coordinate of the divertor
target](name:x_coordinate_of_divertor_target) identifies a Cartesian center
rather than a surface span.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_camera
items.description:
Vertical coordinate of the camera's geometric center, giving its signed
height relative to the origin in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z)
frame.
items.documentation:
Vertical coordinate of the camera's geometric center specifies its signed
height relative to the coordinate origin in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Here $R$ denotes major radius, $\phi$ toroidal angle,
and $Z$ vertical position.

The coordinate is defined by the vertical projection of the center-position
vector:

$$
Z = \mathbf{x}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is the position vector from the coordinate origin to the
camera's geometric center and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along
the symmetry axis in the direction of increasing $Z$.

The reference point is the camera's geometric center, not an individual
pixel or a line-of-sight point. This coordinate is distinct from the
camera's vertical extent and from components of its local orientation
vectors; no averaging over pixels or cameras is implied.

Together with the camera-center major radius and toroidal angle, it
specifies the center position. The [vertical coordinate of an
aperture](name:vertical_coordinate_of_aperture) applies the same projection
to a different object's geometric center.

Sign convention: Positive when the camera center lies above the coordinate
origin in the direction of increasing $Z$.

items.name: trapped_thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Flux-surface-averaged Coulomb-collisional energy transfer from trapped fast
particles to thermal ions of a specified species, summed over all ionic
charge states.
items.documentation:
Trapped thermal-ion collisional power density is the signed volumetric rate
of kinetic-energy transfer from trapped fast or non-Maxwellian particles to
thermal ions, averaged over a magnetic flux surface. Trapped particles
execute guiding-center bounce orbits rather than complete passing transits.
The trapped-orbit restriction applies to the source distribution, not to the
recipient thermal ions.

For source species $a$ and recipient ion species $i$, the exchange is
defined by the recipient kinetic-energy moment of the Coulomb collision
operator:

$$
P_{i,\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \left\langle \sum_q \int \frac{1}{2}m_i v^2 C_{iq,a}[f_{iq}^{\mathrm{th}},f_a^{\mathrm{tr}}](\mathbf{v})\,d^3v \right\rangle
$$

where $P_{i,\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the trapped-source thermal-ion
collisional power density, $q$ labels the recipient ionic charge states,
$m_i$ is the recipient ion mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is recipient velocity, and $v$
is its magnitude. The distribution $f_{iq}^{\mathrm{th}}$ describes thermal
ions of species $i$ in charge state $q$, while $f_a^{\mathrm{tr}}$ is the
trapped part of the source-species distribution. The operator $C_{iq,a}$
gives the collisional time derivative of the recipient distribution due to
that trapped source. The integral covers all recipient velocities; angle
brackets denote the volume-weighted average over an infinitesimally thin
shell between neighboring magnetic flux surfaces.

The quantity applies to one specified recipient ion species and is summed
over all its ionic charge states, not over different ion species. Retaining
one charge-state contribution gives the corresponding [trapped thermal-ion
charge-state collisional power
density](name:trapped_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions).
It is an energy source or sink for the thermal recipient population, not its
stored kinetic-energy density, the source particles' energy-loss rate, or a
volume-integrated power.

Together with the [co-passing
contribution](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions)
and the corresponding counter-passing contribution, it forms the orbit-class
decomposition of the flux-surface average of [thermal-ion collisional power
density](name:thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions), provided the
same source distribution and recipient species are used throughout.

Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb collisions transfer net kinetic
energy from the trapped source population to the thermal ions; negative when
the net transfer is reversed.

items.name: toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Toroidal component of the oxygen impurity ion fluid velocity evaluated at
the H-mode pedestal reference location, projected along the direction of
increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The toroidal oxygen velocity at the pedestal top characterizes the impurity
ion fluid flow projected onto the $\hat{\phi}$ direction at the H-mode edge
transport barrier's outer shoulder, where the steep-gradient pedestal region
transitions to the flatter core profile. Oxygen (atomic number $Z = 8$) is a
common intrinsic or deliberately seeded impurity in tokamaks, present in
charge states spanning O$^{5+}$ through O$^{8+}$ in the pedestal; this
quantity represents the oxygen fluid velocity aggregated over the
predominant charge states unless a specific ionization state is separately
resolved.

The toroidal component is defined by the projection:

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{O}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{O}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing
toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame,
and $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{O}}$ is the oxygen ion fluid velocity vector
evaluated at the pedestal-top locus.

This quantity is measured via charge exchange recombination spectroscopy,
which resolves the Doppler shift of oxygen emission lines following charge
exchange with an injected neutral beam. Toroidal rotation velocities at the
pedestal top in H-mode span roughly $10^3$–$10^5$ m s$^{-1}$, reflecting
neutral beam torque input, intrinsic rotation, and impurity-specific flow
corrections. Comparison with
[toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_pedestal_top](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_pedestal_top)
and
[toroidal_neon_velocity_at_pedestal_top](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_pedestal_top)
enables cross-species benchmarking of pedestal rotation profiles.

Sign convention: Positive when the oxygen ion flow is directed in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: helium_4_density_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Helium-4 ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the
local concentration of helium-4 ions summed over all ionization states.
items.documentation:
Helium-4 ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the
local concentration of helium-4 ions at the inner shoulder of the H-mode
transport barrier.

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{He4}} = \sum_{q=1}^{2} n_{\mathrm{He4}}^{(q)}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{He4}}$ is the helium-4 ion number density,
$n_{\mathrm{He4}}^{(q)}$ is the local number density of helium-4 ions in
charge state $q$, and $q$ is the positive ion charge-state index. The sum
includes singly and doubly ionized helium-4 and excludes neutral helium-4.

This quantity applies specifically to the helium-4 isotope and is evaluated
locally at the pedestal top, whose position is defined by the [normalized
poloidal-flux coordinate at the pedestal
top](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). It is not a
flux-surface average, line-of-sight average, or total ion density.

It is the helium-4 species specialization of [density at the pedestal
top](name:density_at_pedestal_top). It differs from [helium-4 density at the
plasma boundary](name:helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary) because the
latter is evaluated at the plasma-boundary locus, and it is the mass-isotope
counterpart of [helium-3 density at the pedestal
top](name:helium_3_density_at_pedestal_top).

items.name: second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_neutron_detector
items.description:
Second local tangential coordinate of a neutron detector is the signed
coordinate of an outline vertex along the detector’s second local tangential
axis; with the first local tangential coordinate it defines the detector
cross-section vertex in the right-handed detector-local basis (first
tangential, second tangential, plasma-facing normal), where first tangential
points toward increasing φ in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Second local tangential coordinate of a neutron detector is the signed
in-plane coordinate of a neutron-detector outline vertex along the
detector's second local tangential direction. It is a geometric coordinate
of the detector cross section expressed in the detector-local right-handed
orthonormal basis
$(\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1,\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2,\hat{\mathbf{e}}_3)$, whose first
two directions are tangent to the cross-section plane and whose third
direction is the plasma-facing detector normal.

The coordinate is defined by the scalar projection of the vertex
displacement onto the second local tangential direction:

$$
x_2 = (\mathbf{r}_v - \mathbf{r}_0) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_2
$$

where $x_2$ is the second local tangential coordinate of the neutron
detector, $\mathbf{r}_v$ is the position vector of the outline vertex,
$\mathbf{r}_0$ is the neutron-detector local origin, and
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2$ is the second local tangential unit vector.

The local triad is defined by
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2=\hat{\mathbf{e}}_3\times\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1$, with
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_3$ the plasma-facing detector normal and
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1$ the first local tangential direction chosen toward
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame with basis unit vectors
$(\hat{\mathbf{R}},\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}},\hat{\mathbf{Z}})$, where $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ increases counterclockwise when viewed from above
$+\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$, and $Z$ is vertical height. This quantity applies to
individual outline vertices of the neutron-detector cross section; it is not
summed, averaged, or interpreted as an extent over multiple vertices.

Together with the [first local tangential coordinate of a neutron
detector](name:first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_neutron_detector), it
specifies a vertex in the detector cross-section plane; both coordinates are
purely geometric outline coordinates. It is distinct from the detector's
normal extent, such as the [height of a neutron
detector](name:height_of_neutron_detector), from any cylindrical $R$,
$\phi$, or $Z$ position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame,
and from quantities describing detector response or neutron populations.

Sign convention: Positive when the displacement from the neutron-detector
local origin to the outline vertex is in the direction of
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2$, equivalently
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_3\times\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1$.

items.name: y_coordinate_of_ferritic_element_centroid
items.description:
Signed y coordinate of the geometric centroid of a ferritic element in the
right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame, with z aligned to vertical Z.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the signed Cartesian y position of the geometric centroid of
one ferritic element. The coordinate is defined in the right-handed
Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis, with coordinate values
$(x,y,z)$ and $\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$.

$$
y_c = \frac{1}{V_e}\int_{V_e} y\,dV
$$

where $y_c$ and $y$ are Cartesian y coordinates measured in m, $V_e$ is the
ferritic-element volume measured in m$^3$, and $dV$ is a differential volume
element. The integration covers the entire element, so this is a volume
centroid rather than a surface centroid or a selected-point coordinate. The
corresponding orthogonal centroid coordinates are [x coordinate of the
ferritic element centroid](name:x_coordinate_of_ferritic_element_centroid)
and [z coordinate of the ferritic element
centroid](name:z_coordinate_of_ferritic_element_centroid).

Sign convention: Positive when the centroid displacement from the coordinate
origin has a positive projection onto $\hat{y}$.

items.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Effective kinematic coefficient relating diffusive transport of poloidal
flow momentum to flow shear for ions of one species in a specified charge
state.
items.documentation:
This effective kinematic coefficient governs diffusive redistribution of the
poloidal component of [momentum](name:momentum) carried by ions of one
species in a specified ionization state. It enters that charge state's
poloidal momentum balance; the poloidal label identifies the transported
momentum component rather than prescribing transport along a poloidal arc.

In a local velocity-shear closure, the associated diffusive momentum flux
is:

$$
\Pi_{s,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -m_s n_s D_{s,\mathrm{p}}\frac{\partial v_{s,\mathrm{p}}}{\partial \ell}
$$

where $s$ identifies the ion species and charge state, $\mathrm{p}$ denotes
the poloidal component, $\Pi_{s,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the
diffusive flux of that component along the transport direction, $m_s$ is the
ion mass, $n_s$ is the charge-state number density, $D_{s,\mathrm{p}}$ is
this diffusion coefficient, $v_{s,\mathrm{p}}$ is the charge-state mean
poloidal velocity, and $\ell$ is physical distance along the transport
direction specified by the closure.

The poloidal direction is tangent to a magnetic flux surface at fixed
toroidal angle in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, where $\rho$ labels
flux surfaces, $\theta$ is the poloidal angle, and $\phi$ is the toroidal
angle. The coefficient is charge-state resolved, not summed or averaged over
charge states, and is not restricted to an edge region.

It specializes the [momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:momentum_diffusion_coefficient) to poloidal flow momentum
and a specified ion charge state. The velocity-shear closure acts on the
charge-state poloidal velocity gradient, not the gradient of total plasma
momentum density. It excludes advective transport, represented separately by
the [ion charge-state momentum convection
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity), as well as
residual stress and external momentum sources.

items.name: neutral_internal_state_energy_flux
items.description:
