Neutral internal-state energy flux is the net thermal energy transported per
unit area and time across an oriented surface by one neutral species in one
specified internal state.
items.documentation:
Neutral internal-state energy flux describes thermal-energy transport across
an oriented surface by neutral particles of one species in one specified
internal state. It is direction-agnostic: the surface orientation determines
which projection of the transport is represented.

The local flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{0,s,W} = \frac{\partial^2 W_{0,s}^{\mathrm{net}}}{\partial A\,\partial t} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{0,s,W}\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}
$$

where $\Gamma_{0,s,W}$ is the signed surface-normal thermal-energy flux,
$W_{0,s}^{\mathrm{net}}$ is the net thermal energy transferred through the
surface, $A$ is surface area, $t$ is time, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{0,s,W}$ is
the corresponding thermal-energy transport vector, and $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is
the chosen surface unit normal. The subscripts $0$, $s$, and $W$ identify
the neutral population, specified internal state, and energy channel,
respectively.

The quantity is not summed over internal states or neutral species and is
not restricted to a single transport mechanism. It is a flux density, not a
surface-integrated power or particle-number flux; the internal-state label
selects the carrier population rather than identifying an excitation-energy
flux.

Summing the underlying transport vectors over all internal states of the
same species gives the [neutral-species energy
flux](name:neutral_species_energy_flux). The [poloidal
flux](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_flux) and [field-parallel
flux](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_flux) are projections of
the same state-resolved transport vector onto the local poloidal direction
and local magnetic-field direction, respectively.

Sign convention: Positive when net thermal energy carried by the selected
neutral population crosses the surface in the direction of the chosen unit
normal.

items.name: poloidal_neutral_energy_diffusivity
items.description:
Effective poloidal diffusivity for neutral thermal-energy transport,
relating the diffusive energy flux tangent to constant-ρ surfaces to the
local poloidal gradient of neutral energy density.
items.documentation:
Poloidal neutral energy diffusivity is the effective diagonal transport
coefficient for diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by neutral
atoms and molecules along the poloidal direction.

In flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, its defining constitutive relation
is

$$
q_{n,\theta}^{\mathrm{diff}}=-D_{n,\theta}\frac{\partial u_n}{\partial s_\theta}
$$

where $q_{n,\theta}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the poloidal diffusive
neutral-energy flux density, $D_{n,\theta}$ is the poloidal diffusivity,
$u_n$ is neutral thermal-energy density, and $s_\theta$ is physical
arclength along the poloidal tangent at fixed $\rho$ and $\phi$. The
diffusivity has units of m$^2$ s$^{-1}$, while $s_\theta$ is measured in m.

This quantity is the poloidal specialization of [neutral energy
diffusivity](name:effective_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient). It
aggregates the relevant neutral populations and is distinct from the
state-resolved [poloidal neutral internal-state energy
diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusivity).

items.name: volume_averaged_boron_density
items.description:
Volume-averaged boron density is the elemental boron number density
integrated over the plasma volume and divided by that volume, including
every boron charge state.
items.documentation:
Volume-averaged boron density is the elemental boron particle density
averaged over the plasma volume, with neutral boron and every ionic charge
state included.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_B = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_B(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $\overline{n}_B$ is the volume-averaged quantity, $V_p$ is the plasma
volume, $n_B(\mathbf{r})$ is the local [boron density](name:boron_density),
and $\mathbf{r}$ specifies position. The local density includes all boron
charge states through $n_B=\sum_{Z=0}^{5}n_{B,Z}$, where $Z$ is the ionic
charge state and $n_{B,Z}$ is the density in that state.

This is a global volume average, distinct from the local boron density and
from the [ratio of volume-averaged boron density to volume-averaged electron
density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_boron_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density),
which expresses the same boron content relative to the electron population.

items.name: vertical_displacement_of_beamlet_group
items.description:
Signed vertical displacement of a neutral-beam-injection beamlet-group
center from its static geometry during dynamic beam tilting.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the signed change in the vertical position of a
beamlet-group center when the beamlet geometry is dynamically tilted away
from its static configuration. It represents the group center as a geometric
object, not the beamlet group's extent or focal length.

The displacement is defined by

$$
\Delta Z = Z_{\mathrm{dynamic}} - Z_{\mathrm{static}}
$$

where $\Delta Z$ is the vertical displacement, $Z_{\mathrm{dynamic}}$ is the
vertical coordinate of the beamlet-group center in the dynamically tilted
configuration, and $Z_{\mathrm{static}}$ is its corresponding coordinate in
the static geometry. These coordinates are expressed in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The scope is one beamlet group treated as a single geometric object during
dynamic tilting; the quantity is a center displacement rather than a
per-beamlet value, an absolute position, or a displacement summed over
beamlet properties. It excludes the group's cross-sectional size, which is
described by its [vertical width](name:vertical_width_of_beamlet_group), and
its distance to a focal point, described by its [vertical focal
length](name:vertical_focal_length_of_beamlet_group).

The quantity is the vertical counterpart of a signed radial center
displacement such as [radial offset of a beamlet
group](name:radial_offset_of_beamlet_group). It differs from [perturbed
major radius](name:perturbed_major_radius), which describes dynamic
variation of a beam-line tangency radius rather than the vertical position
of the beamlet-group center.

Sign convention: Positive when the dynamically tilted beamlet-group center
is displaced toward increasing $Z$.

items.name: deuterium_prefill_count
items.description:
Deuterium prefill count is the total amount of neutral deuterium introduced
before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with one
count unit per atom.
items.documentation:
Deuterium prefill count is the total amount of neutral deuterium (D)
introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an
equivalent-electron count. Each neutral deuterium atom contributes one
equivalent electron.

The equivalent-electron count is obtained by accumulating injected deuterium
atoms over the prefill interval and weighting them by the deuterium atomic
number:

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{D,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{D}} N_{\mathrm{D,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{D}} \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{D}}(t)\,dt = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{D}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{D,prefill}}$ is the equivalent-electron
count, $N_{\mathrm{D,prefill}}$ is the accumulated neutral-deuterium atom
count, $Z_{\mathrm{D}}=1$ is the deuterium atomic number,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{D}}$ is the deuterium atom injection rate, $t_0$ is the
prefill start time, and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time.

This quantity includes only deuterium introduced before breakdown and
excludes wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas
injection, and retained or ionized inventory. It is the deuterium-specific
component of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count) and uses the same
isotope-resolved convention as tritium_prefill_count.

items.name: cold_neutral_fraction
items.description:
Dimensionless fraction of the cold recycled component of a hydrogen-isotope
neutral population relative to the total neutral atom population.
items.documentation:
The cold neutral fraction is a dimensionless ratio bounded in $[0, 1]$
expressing the relative abundance of the cold, low-energy recycled component
of a hydrogen-isotope neutral population. It is a component of the broader
[neutral
fraction](name:ratio_of_neutral_state_density_to_total_hydrogenic_density),
distinct from the hot charge-exchange-born component.

The fraction is defined as:

$$
f_{\mathrm{cold}} = \frac{n_{\mathrm{cold}}}{n_{\mathrm{cold}} + n_{\mathrm{hot}}}
$$

where $f_{\mathrm{cold}}$ is the cold neutral fraction, $n_{\mathrm{cold}}$
is the number density of cold recycled neutral atoms, and $n_{\mathrm{hot}}$
is the number density of hot charge-exchange-born neutral atoms.

The quantity applies to a specified hydrogen isotope and uses the
two-component neutral-population model. Its denominator is the total neutral
population formed by the cold and hot components for that isotope; it is not
summed across different isotopes and does not represent the hot component
itself.

Within this model, the cold and hot fractions are complementary and sum to
unity. The [hot neutral fraction](name:hot_neutral_fraction) gives the
corresponding charge-exchange-born component, with the energy threshold
separating the two components defined by the applicable population model.

items.name: non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field
items.description:
Non-axisymmetric magnetic-field vector of the local vacuum induction
generated by external coils, with its toroidally averaged component removed.
items.documentation:
The non-axisymmetric magnetic field $\mathbf{B}_{\rm NA}$ is the vector part
of the external-coil vacuum [magnetic induction](name:magnetic_field) that
varies with toroidal angle after its toroidally averaged component is
removed. It retains the full field direction rather than selecting a
cylindrical component or a magnitude.

The non-axisymmetric component is defined by

$$
\mathbf{B}_{\rm NA}(R,\phi,Z) = \mathbf{B}_{\rm vac}(R,\phi,Z) - \left\langle \mathbf{B}_{\rm vac} \right\rangle_\phi(R,Z)
$$

where $\mathbf{B}_{\rm NA}$ is the non-axisymmetric magnetic induction,
$\mathbf{B}_{\rm vac}$ is the magnetic induction generated by external coil
currents with plasma-current contributions omitted, and $\langle
\mathbf{B}_{\rm vac} \rangle_\phi$ is its average over the toroidal angle.
The variables $R$, $\phi$, and $Z$ are respectively major radius, toroidal
angle, and vertical height in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame.

This quantity is a local vector field defined for the external-coil vacuum
contribution, without restriction to a particular plasma population or
spatial region. Its aggregation convention is the removal of the
toroidal-angle average, so only non-axisymmetric toroidal variation remains.

It excludes the toroidally symmetric vacuum field, magnetic induction
generated by plasma currents, and any scalar magnitude reduction. It
therefore does not represent the full local [magnetic
induction](name:magnetic_field) when those omitted source contributions are
present.

The vector is the common parent for its cylindrical projections: the [radial
non-axisymmetric magnetic
field](name:radial_non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field), [toroidal
non-axisymmetric magnetic
field](name:toroidal_non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field), and [vertical
non-axisymmetric magnetic
field](name:vertical_non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field) each resolve this same
vector along one direction of the right-handed cylindrical frame.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved component points along its
corresponding positive basis direction in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.
